Appearance: Johnny is a young man with a well-built upper body but paralyzed legs. He has light eyes, and light, shoulder-length hair curling upwards at its ends. Johnny almost always wears a knit cap, printed with many small five-pointed stars. His hair sticks out of holes on either side of the top, taking a shape like short horns. A horseshoe hangs from the front, framing an image of the dark silhouette of the profile of a horse's reared head. When Johnny uses his Stand Tusk, small stars appear on his hands. While it is not seen, Johnny bears the Star Birthmark, as Lucy Steel is aware of it. After being shot by Funny Valentine, he bears a scar on each cheek for the remainder of the battle with the president.

Throughout the Steel Ball Run race, Johnny gradually changes into a more realistic appearance, with slightly wavy hair and a slightly fuller build. At the same time, he dons various outfits to suit the weather across America, each outfit retaining the star patterns of his hat and legs and the stripes on his torso.

As a paraplegic, Johnny uses a wheelchair before the race begins. During the race, however, he is usually mounted on his horse, Slow Dancer. He is the only mounted competitor in the Steel Ball Run who spends the majority of the race without using his stirrups; instead, his legs remain tucked and tied against the horse's flanks, or are sometimes secured to the saddle to prevent him from falling.

Personality: Johnny Joestar is introduced as a distant, depressive paraplegic man whose career as a horse jockey was ruined when he was shot in the spine after conceitedly antagonizing a passerby. However, after he momentarily experiences the ability to stand on his feet after touching the Steel Balls of Gyro Zeppeli, he becomes determined to follow Gyro and, through his guidance, learn the Spin for himself. Later, having his legs twitch due to the Corpse Parts, he additionally sets out to acquire them, despite the many other murderous pursuers of the same goal.

Two of Johnny's most defining characteristics carried from his introduction through most of the race are his frequently egocentric behavior and his strong resolve. His fame and fortune from his success as a horse jockey made him exceedingly arrogant and self-indulgent, and the paralysis of his legs only somewhat subdued his selfishness, as shown when he aggressively disregards the well-being of passersby when he first encounters and pursues Gyro. His intense desire to regain feeling in his legs motivates him to enter the Steel Ball Run race and do whatever he deems necessary to achieve his goal, including enduring severe wounds. One notable instance is when he desperately attempts to ride a horse for an entire day straight, which leaves him with many bloody injuries and even almost gets him trampled to death. When Johnny discovers the Saint's Corpse and again feels his legs move, he becomes even more fiercely resolute in his goal to participate in the race and restore the use of his legs, now by finding the rest of the Corpse Parts. Due to the conspiracy surrounding the Corpse that inevitably involves him with a variety of people, Johnny's selfishness reaches a peak as he puts his own goal above all others', and he consistently displays few qualms about being violent or killing his opponents to get the Corpse Parts. As described by Ringo Roadagain and later by Gyro, Johnny has a "dark determination" in his eyes that motivates him to kill in cold blood and throw his morals in general if the perceived need arises, and this can be seen when he ruthlessly tries to kill his opponents and even almost destroys a Corpse Part so that no one else can have it.

Johnny is not completely amoral, however, and his experiences in the Steel Ball Run race help him to overcome his self-centeredness. He generally holds on to basic morals in regards to others in most situations, for instance objecting to involve the defenseless Lucy Steel in their struggle for the Corpse due to her young age and the incredible riskiness of Gyro's plan. His growing bond with Gyro Zeppeli as a close friend ultimately proves most integral to his maturation. Although his intense desire for the Corpse and the use of his legs almost motivates him to sacrifice Gyro in one instance, he manages to eventually discard his own selfish desires for once to prevent Gyro from being damned by Sugar Mountain. Johnny momentarily hesitates to kill Funny Valentine after defeating him due to Valentine's speech about his supposedly noble intentions and Johnny's own selfish desire to see Gyro again through a variant of him from a Parallel World, but in the end, his friendship with Gyro and the example Gyro led as a truly noble person help him to distinguish right from wrong and put an end to the president's evil. Subsequently, Johnny's growth continues when the complete Corpse is suddenly stolen and culminates in the establishment of his first selfless goal, to defeat whoever stole it and prevent whatever misfortune may come from their theft as the only one capable of doing so.

During the Steel Ball Run race, Johnny is burdened by depression and a subsequent lack of confidence. Notably calling himself a useless person, Johnny's bleak outlook on life stems from his youth. Johnny was a timid yet kind child during his childhood, adopting a wild mouse and calling it Danny. Though he was afraid of his harsh father George Joestar, he would try to live up to his expectations. Johnny idolized his older brother Nicholas. When Nicholas died after falling from a horse that was seemingly startled by Danny, Johnny became guilt-ridden, believing that his brother's death was his fault and that he should have died instead. He then believed throughout the years that fate itself was taking revenge on him for his crime and that every misfortune he received was deserved. This results in his obsession with the blessing of the Corpse, which would reset his karma to a neutral state of "zero" instead of the "negative" state of his curse. It also explains Johnny's rampant lack of confidence and near-constant bouts of panic, thinking that fate could take away his hope of acquiring the Corpse at any moment. When Johnny's father disowned him, Johnny shut himself off, creating a facade of conceitedness to hide the sadness this rejection caused him.

Johnny's perspective improves greatly upon meeting Gyro Zeppeli. Having met someone who gives him hope and is genuinely nice to him, Johnny feels grateful for meeting the Italian executioner and treasures this relationship, at one point being willing to abandon the Corpse Parts he has to save his friend. Gyro repeatedly knocks Johnny out of his lack of confidence and helps him get the Corpse Parts, giving him assurance and optimism in life.

As reflected in the multiple ACTs of his Stand Tusk, Johnny's improvement in his self-esteem is gradual. The key steps of his progress include Johnny discovering the Corpse (ACT1), then standing up for himself against Soundman (ACT2), symbolically cleansing himself of his guilt against Axl RO and being blessed by Jesus Christ's apparition (ACT3) and finally acquiring the Corpse and regaining the use of his legs (ACT4). Although Gyro dies, Johnny cherishes the time they spent together. During the race, Johnny is uncaring of everyone else save himself and Gyro, only maintaining a polite but cold demeanor at best toward the people he meets. However, Gyro's influence makes Johnny slightly more friendly toward people, culminating in his marriage with Rina Higashikata.
Johnny reveals to Gyro that he has a paraphilia for women with bug bites, which he is deeply embarrassed by and keeps secret.

In JoJolion, a flashback shows that Johnny found happiness during his short life with Rina. When his wife was stricken with the Rock Disease and he was unable to find any cure, Johnny experienced a lapse in character due to his sorrow and desperation over the matter, returning to the selfishness that had plagued him in the past. Seeing his son afflicted with the disease as a result of his selfish misuse of the Holy Corpse returned him to his senses and revealed a stronger-than-ever sense of selflessness. His growth of character that culminated from his journeys with Gyro and his marriage with Rina was enough that he was willing to sacrifice his own life to cure his son and ensure that nobody else would receive the brunt of the Equivalent Exchange.
Abilities: Spin / Stand

Johnny first seeks Gyro Zeppeli's tutelage in the ways of the Spin in order to regain the use of his legs. Most often, Johnny channels the Spin by the use of his Stand, Tusk; developed first with the power of the Corpse's left hand, and further with Gyro's help. Its form varies, depending on the sort or style of Spin Johnny chooses to employ.
ACT1

Tusk ACT1 is awakened in the Devil's Palm when the corpse part combines itself with Johnny's left hand, manifesting his Stand with the ability to spin his nails and fire them akin to bullets, and regrowing his nails in seconds.
ACT2

Tusk ACT2 manifests when Johnny shoots a nail whilst incorporating the Golden Rectangle in a fight against Sandman. Despite the longer regrow time, the nails possess more power and a new ability that lets the holes of the bullets follow the target for a small amount of time.
ACT3

Tusk ACT3 is the final "base" form for Tusk and manifests when Johnny shoots himself with a Golden Rectangle-empowered nail, enabling him to transfer parts of his body through the holes to shoot from different directions. It was awakened by advice from Jesus Christ in a fight against Axl RO.
ACT4

Tusk ACT4 manifests itself as a result of Johnny utilizing Slow Dancer's power combined with the golden rectangle, which enables Johnny to fire Golden Spin nail-bullets that have infinite rotation. ACT4 possesses the power to force open D4C Love Train's dimensional wall, and trap anyone hit by it to a single spot indefinitely.
Horseback Riding

Johnny Joestar has been described as a genius jockey, being one of the favorites of the Steel Ball Run race. His skill allows him to ride across many types of terrain, and challenge even fellow genius jockey Diego Brando. Johnny possesses great knowledge of his horse Slow Dancer, notably its abilities and limits, being able to gauge what Slow Dancer will be capable of at any moment.

Appearance: Gyro is a man of average to above-average height and medium to athletic build. He has long hair that reaches mid-back, light-colored eyes, and square patches of facial hair lining his jaw, four on each side. He either wears grills or has chiseled into prosthetic teeth the phrase "GO! GO! ZEPPELI", which are said to be gold.

Throughout the Steel Ball Run race, Gyro wears a variety of outfits to suit the weather of the current location. However, they all maintain the same key elements and motifs of his wide-brimmed hat and slit goggles, a dark shirt studded with miniature steel balls, a cape wrapped around his shoulders that splits into three segments, and his large belt with a two-piece belt buckle, engraved with a pair of hands pointing down towards his crotch. His belt is equipped with special holsters for his two Steel Balls.

Personality: Gyro is a cocky and flamboyant executioner marked by the harshness of life, who participates in the Steel Ball Run for the sake of Marco.

Gyro initially appears as an aggressive contestant in the Steel Ball Run race. Unlike other competitors, Gyro looks to seize first place above all else, rushing ahead of everyone and then fending off anyone who challenges him. He also has a tendency to take dangerous shortcuts. Gyro is a rude man, deriding the vast majority of those he meets with insults and mocking commentaries. Even with his closest friend Johnny Joestar, Gyro doesn't mince his words and sometimes argues with him. Moreover, Johnny only made a lasting impression on Gyro through his dogged stubbornness and otherwise looked down on him during their first meeting. The only person for whom Gyro had any degree of respect is his stern father Gregorio Zeppeli. Gyro's overconfidence extends to his fights, during which Gyro is prone to mock his enemies in some way or say something brash. For instance, he openly mocked Mountain Tim's "ridiculous" hat.

Gyro is particularly proud of his mastery of the Spin, a family technique involving the rotation and throwing of steel balls to various effects, and hails the Spin as the acme of human skill, this pride is, to a degree, justified when the Spin manages to overpower D4C Love Train. However, as a teacher he seemed to be somewhat begrudging, only bothering to teach Johnny the basics of the Spin and introducing him to the Golden Rectangle when they were threatened by a new enemy.

As an executioner and otherwise confrontational man, Gyro is not afraid to use violence even in a lethal fashion. However, Gyro doesn't have the same ruthlessness as Johnny and initially doesn't seek to kill his enemies if he deems it unnecessary. Notably, Gyro did try to discourage a thief from fighting with him and only used his Steel Balls to make the man shoot himself if he ever drew his gun, instead of directly killing him.

Gyro nonetheless possesses an altruistic side, and likes to help anyone who needs his assistance, most notably the paraplegic, Johnny, to whom he taught the Spin technique and helped acquire the Holy Corpse Parts, or Marco, the helpless child whose death sentence Gyro seeks to appeal by winning the Steel Ball Run. Gyro would often clash this side with the authority of Gregorio Zeppeli, who disapproved of any display of sentimentality in life and ultimately defied him by going to America.

Johnny originally said that Gyro didn't have the drive and determination necessary to get things done. The jockey argued that because Gyro inherited everything he had as an upperclassman and heir of the family Spin technique, he didn't have the kind of selfish hunger born from suffering which was crucial in the race. True to that, Gyro Zeppeli initially raced out of altruistic concern for Marco, and primarily relied on tricks to prevail in the race. During his battle with Ringo Roadagain he bent his original motivations into a more personal goal, the path to see for himself whether Marco deserved to be executed and who exactly the Corpse was. After that, Gyro switched to a slightly less cocky behavior, and focused seriously on his battles. In his horse riding, Gyro switched to a more personal style, instinctively choosing his own route instead of the "shortest path", enabling him to even outmatch Diego in the race.

Out of combat, Gyro also possesses an eccentric personality and is particularly bombastic. Gyro has a penchant for gags, involving puns or an inexplicable brand of humor from bad puns to skits defying all logic, frequently telling such jokes to Johnny in the spur of the moment and created a song about Mozzarella cheese, singing it to Johnny and being happy that he appreciated it. He also has a fondness for dramatic gestures and quotes, saying that the Goddess of Victory was riding with him and that she would retract her favor if he ever let another woman ride with him. Unlike Johnny, Gyro frequently grins, exposing his metal teeth in the process. The mere fact that he engraved his teeth with the message "Go! Go! Zeppeli" already exposes his ostentatious nature. Humorously, Gyro also keeps a pink teddy bear with him, being fond of it enough to keep it even during the Steel Ball Run, although he leaves it at one point. However, mimicking his own father, Gyro can be stern and dignified when he talks about the Zeppeli Spin technique.

Heavily influenced by Gregorio's teachings about the uncertainties in life - using a "tennis ball over the net" metaphor - and the Steel Ball's power being nothing short of miraculous, Gyro has a somewhat optimistic outlook on life and is convinced that he can overcome setbacks, even if they'd need a miracle to overcome, as long as he follows a virtuous path. Nonetheless, following the "tennis ball over the net" belief, Gyro is aware that failure is just as likely. This ideology is repeatedly somehow confirmed with numerous coincidences and miracles helping him throughout his journey and alternatively working against him, culminating in Marco being freed without his intervention but dying of a cold later.

Gyro is a womanizer, one flashback narrating an affair with a patient and he is shown flirting with pretty girls. On the other hand, the first time Gyro and Johnny meet Lucy, he refuses to let her ride with him and states that "no woman (will) ride my horse". He later explains that the "Goddess of Victory" would be jealous if he let "another woman" ride with him.

Gyro has a few tics of language. For instance, he has a signature "Nyo-ho-ho!" chuckle and he usually shouts out "ORA!" when he hurls a Steel Ball in combat, reminiscent of the Stand Cries of the former Joestar Stands. Eventually, after Gyro's death, Johnny adopts Gyro's battle cry as Tusk ACT4's own Stand Rush.
Abilities: Gyro is an adept tactician, being able to hold his own against several Stand users and outsmarting them in several occasions. Gyro has been shown to be able to use his surroundings, or even the enemy's own power to his advantage. He is also a worldly individual, possessing a range of knowledge, including in tracking, opera, paleontology, and mathematics.

Trained by his father, Gregorio Zeppeli, Gyro is an accomplished surgeon, being able to make surgical operations on his own. This training also includes intimate knowledge of the human body Gyro uses in conjunction with the Spin in combat.
Steel Ball / Spin
Scan

Scan (スキャン, Sukyan) is an ability of the Steel Ball[a] that Gyro temporarily awakens to after possessing the Corpse's right eye. The Right Eye is protected by a Guardian Spirit composed of energy which is shown emerging from Gyro's Steel Ball when he uses Scan in his battle against Ringo Roadagain.

The word "TURBŌ" is inscribed on Gyro's iris with a diagonally oriented cross behind it, and a cross pattée emerges below his eye, on his cheek. Inside the letters are binary numbers corresponding to the location of the next Corpse Part.

When Scan is active, the ability places a single eye also marked with the word "TURBO" on each of Gyro's active Steel Balls. Scan enhances both Gyro's aptitude for the Spin and his vision. It improves his capability of targeting body parts or analyzing his enemy's weaknesses by acting as a remote camera or surrogate eyes. When the Steel Ball strikes the ground, the Spin's vibration allows echolocation-based vision. For instance, Scan allows Gyro to discover an old wound on Ringo Roadagain's collarbone, and lets him see Hot Pants's spine remotely to immobilize her arms with the Spin when she blinds him with Cream Starter.
Gyro relinquishes this ability when he gives the eye to Lucy Steel.
Stand

Ball Breaker manifests when Gyro finally achieves the Golden Spin. The Stand is a visualization of Spin energy unleashed from Gyro's Steel Balls, the sheer power of the technique manifesting itself into the form of a Stand. Ball Breaker embodies a vast force capable of bypassing dimensional barriers.

Although he does not manifest a Stand until much later, Gyro is able to see Stands as early as his encounter with Andre Boomboom, and his Steel Ball technique becomes noticeably stronger after passing through the Devil's Palm.
Horseback Riding

Gyro is an experienced and capable equestrian, competent enough to ride across many types of terrain and be a serious competitor in the Steel Ball Run race. His ability as a rider reached a new level after he entered a "real man's world" in his fight against Ringo Roadagain and he became able to instinctively choose the optimal path for his horse, an ability that seems on par with Diego Brando's own ability. His riding style can be summed up as aggressive; Gyro seeks to remain at the first place constantly, and takes dangerous shortcuts when he deems it necessary. When another rider challenges him, Gyro will actively try to get rid of them. His beloved horse is named Valkyrie. Gyro is also knowledgeable about horses, particularly Valkyrie, whose abilities and limits he can gauge at any moment.

Lucy is a fourteen-year-old girl of average height and build. She has light, medium-length hair and an outfit generally consisting of a dress and striped tights. She also wears arm warmers and tall boots, both adorned with circular decorations.

Later, after she is kidnapped by Funny Valentine, her outfit is simplified to only a dress and a pair of pumps, and her hair is slightly longer than before. During her final appearance, Lucy is seen wearing a hood, while also regaining her arm warmers and boots but without any tights underneath.

Personality: Lucy is an intelligent, gentle and courageous girl despite facing many dangerous situations.

Already apparent in her childhood, Lucy's kindness pushed her to talk to a then derelict Steven Steel, being the first person to support him in his idea of organizing a horserace and also suggesting that it had an enormous scale by making it go across the United States and having a prize in the millions. When Steven repaid her kindness by preventing the mafia from taking her away, Lucy was deeply grateful to Steven, developing a deep relationship with him although it would remain platonic despite everyone else's bias.

Lucy isn't shown interacting much with other people, usually being rather withdrawn compared to Steven's bombastic public persona. However, she is the only one who knows about his moments of doubt and sadness and during them encourages her husband. When interacting with other people, Lucy usually acts polite and rather meek.

As Steven's wife, Lucy is extremely loyal to him and her every action during the course of the Steel Ball Run is performed in order to protect him from danger. As such, despite being a frail and Stand-less person, Lucy constantly throws herself into dangerous actions without hesitation. Not only does she infiltrate several well-protected facilities in order to undermine Funny Valentine, she also has several perilous encounters against Stand users such as Blackmore, Mike O. or even Diego Brando, all of whom try to kill her. She also plainly rejects Mountain Tim's advances, stating her pride in being Steven's wife.

Although she is prone to nervousness, Lucy is also an extremely resourceful girl, being adept at tricking people or performing other tricks to escape notice. She knows lip-reading and is a competent actor, which in conjunction with her status as the main promoter's wife, allows her to access several usually secure places. Even on the brink of capture or worse, Lucy can think of ways to escape using all available tools and allies. Lucy is ultimately the one who defeats Diego Brando by bringing his alternate self's head to him, killing him in spite of his formidable Stand. Despite her gentle nature, Lucy also doesn't hesitate to fire at Blackmore or stab Valentine, showing a hidden ruthless side to her.

Much later in her life, Lucy gained a spot in the Speedwagon Foundation as a botanist and geomorphologist. She is an accomplished scientist, able to use her knowledge out in the field while investigating the Locacaca. Lucy is still kind and courageous, offering Joseph Joestar a job and investigating an ominous guard-rail. With age, she developed a philosophy around the idea of a purpose, or mission, chosen by a greater force that one latches onto to complete.
Abilities: Stand

Funny Valentine identifies Lucy as compatible with the Saint's Corpse and catalyzes a fusion and metamorphosis between the two. A temporary Stand is created after the corpse fuses itself with Lucy, gathering inside her and taking over her bodily functions. While enacted, the Stand provides divine protection, which Funny uses to his advantage during his fight with the protagonists.
Lip-Reading

Lucy is a lip reader, enabling her to spy on people and determine what they are saying purely through lip movement. It allowed her to know about the secret message Ringo Roadagain sent to Valentine and intercept it before the President.

His attire usually consists of a high collared coat decorated with several tassels on the collar and assorted pants. Steven also wears small rectangular glasses with dark lenses.

Personality: Steven Steel is shown to be an anxious character despite bearing a bold facade as the organizer and host of the Steel Ball Run race. During most of his life, Steven Steel has cultivated a bombastic and eccentric persona, becoming a performer, sportsman and other jobs in the center of the stage, but would find his calling as a promoter for various events. Despite the ups and downs of his career, Steven has managed to always rebound to success. Steven also projects the image of a stern and confident promoter who tackles any problem with calm and authority. When a clerk reports numerous problems during the preparations, Steven calmly raises the budget and orders to make it clear troublemakers will be thrown out. Privately, Steven is full of doubts and only dreams of a modest amount of fame, being content that a paper would print his name even at the bottom of the page as long his contribution was acknowledged. All these thoughts he only shares with Lucy.

Steven Steel is a romantic man holding several ideals. He notably promotes the Steel Ball Run as a testament to mankind's pioneer spirit, intending to make it so for the first time, a lone man crosses the United States with his horse and accepting all other vehicles used in the race as a challenge to this spirit. He also considers that "true failure" is to abandon this pioneer spirit and avoid hardships. Steven Steel is also content with the bit of fame his events grant him but doesn't seem to be after monetary gains, as he offered all of the profit from the race to various causes and also refused to throw a fight during his career as a boxer, even if he was shot in the knee by gangsters. Steven also made the effort to save Lucy from the mafia as repayment for her support.

Steven has a privileged and platonic relationship with his wife, Lucy. Having once fallen in love during his youth, Steven was thrown into despair by the death of his fiancé and promised to never love again. True to that, despite being Lucy's husband and everyone considering her as a trophy wife for a salacious old man, Steven never touches her and considers her as his protegee. As she was the first to encourage him during an all-time low in his career and he saved her from the hands of gangsters, Steven and Lucy share a great affection and trust with each other. Steven is so attached to Lucy, he doesn't hesitate to risk his life to save her.

Steven is a reluctant accomplice to Funny Valentine in finding the Saint Corpse Parts, having accepted to collaborate although he was unaware of the violence of the operation. Although he knows about them and has a vague idea of their power, Steel remains uninterested in them during the whole race.
Abilities: Promoting: Steven is a talented promoter, having to his name several bizarre events that he promoted and became popular stories with the public, which made him rich. Steven is also partly responsible for the popularity of the Steel Ball Run race. As a public relations expert, he's given inspiring speeches and arranged things so that journalists would regularly be able to observe and report the race.

Horse riding: Steven Steel is a gifted horseman. Having joined the cavalry but soon retiring from the army because of an illness, his skills would never be put to profit during his life. However, his horse riding skill becomes crucial when he comes to save Johnny, struck by his own ability, and thus shows that he can ride a horse perfectly and allows Johnny to perform another Golden Spin.

Appearance: Diego is a man with a slim to medium build. He has light hair, dark eyebrows, and light, sharp eyes.

He commonly wears an equestrian helmet with the letters "DIO" loosely mounted on bending pins emerging from a small ribbon tied at its front, a turtleneck jumper patterned with a diagonal grid, light, mid-forearm-length gloves, jodhpurs with flared hips, and tall, dark riding boots.

After obtaining the Corpse's left eye and fusing it with his own, his left eye's iris has the word "TURBO" engraved on it, and he temporarily gains a mark under said eye reading "DIO", contrasting to the cross Gyro gains from the right eye.
Color Schemes
Personality: During his childhood, Diego was a good-natured and resourceful kid. His mother raised him with love and taught him to keep his dignity in even the direst situation. At age five, witnessing his mother sacrificing her hands so that he could be fed, Diego developed a resentment of everyone around him for allowing that to happen, and an insatiable ambition.

Since then Diego has been driven to climb the social ladder in order to get back at everyone who wronged him in the past. Upon hearing about the Corpse, he first sought them for himself and as soon as he found himself in a disadvantageous position with a crippled horse, didn't waste time in proposing his services to Funny Valentine, demanding mayorship of Manhattan in exchange for his participation. He harbors a grudge against his biological father Dario, and was ready to cooperate with Hot Pants when she proposed to tell him about his whereabouts.

Using any opportunity, he is said to have married an old woman for her wealth, and in the same vein, participated in the Steel Ball Run for prestige. Diego is particularly vindictive against anyone who gets in his way, and doesn't hesitate to injure or kill them, although he doesn't manifest murderous intents automatically. For instance, at one point during the race he warns Gyro to stay away from him as the latter tried to attack him.

Diego possesses a strong misanthropy, describing humanity as a "flock of pigeons", and resents humans as a whole for the death of his mother. Thus Diego is naturally solitary, never looking to bond with anyone, and in case he has to cooperate with someone, he will keep a certain amount of separation between them. Diego sees human life as worthless and will sacrifice anyone to further his goals without hesitation. For instance, he allowed Wekapipo to be killed by D4C's ability in order to escape.
Abilities: Stand
Diego first turned into a dinosaur after he, along with a number of villagers, were controlled by Dr. Ferdinand in order to steal the left eye of the Saint's Corpse from Johnny and Gyro.

After Ferdinand was defeated, Diego stole the corpse part and fused it with his left eye, allowing him to retain the ability to turn himself into a dinosaur. While initially benefiting from just enhanced senses and strength, the Stand and all of its abilities eventually became his own.
Horseback Riding

Diego is one of the most talented jockeys of his generation and considered a champion candidate in the Steel Ball Run alongside his horse Silver Bullet. His exceptional riding skills allow him to navigate a wide variety of terrain with ease, employing advanced techniques such as drafting behind other horses to reduce air resistance and gain an advantage.

Beyond his riding prowess, Diego possesses an extraordinary ability to analyze both horses and their riders. Diego can assess not only his own horse's capabilities but also those of his competitors, giving him a strategic edge. He notably identifies and exploits the habits and weaknesses of Gyro Zeppeli's horse, Valkyrie, allowing him to get a temporary lead. As a dinosaur, his analytical abilities extend further with his enhanced senses, allowing him to read subtle terrain shifts and horse behavior precisely, including the horse's breath rate, pulse rate, perspiration, and stride length.

personagens.resumo: Hot Pants (ホット・パンツ, Hotto Pantsu) is a secondary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run. She serves as a tertiary antagonist to Gyro and Johnny, and as a secondary ally to Lucy Steel.

ja_kanji.texto: ホット・パンツ

goals.texto: Cleanse herself of her sin using the Saint's Corpse

family.texto: Unnamed Parents | Unnamed Younger Brother

cod.texto: Multiple lacerations of the heart and vital organs via D4C Love Train

seiyuu.texto: Yoko Hikasa (Anime) | Megumi Toyoguchi (Eyes of Heaven)

Appearance: Hot Pants is a woman of above-average height, medium build, and short straight hair. However, her androgynous traits and loose clothes allow her to pass off as a man. According to Araki, Hot Pants binds her breasts to appear more masculine.

Hot Pants's whole body is covered by a baggy striped suit that is further covered with a long blouse. It is decorated with metallic decorations of flowers and leaves, is lined with fur, and has a second layer of cloth covering Hot Pants's chest. Hot Pants also has various accessories such as a fur cap decorated with a single spike at its top, furred elbow pads, and assorted leg warmers. She also wears a belt bearing the letters "HP".
Hot Pants keeps Cream Starter in two holsters located on both sides of her hip.
Color Schemes
Personality: Hot Pants is introduced as a rough and vindictive individual, accusing Johnny and Gyro of stealing her supplies and immediately attacking them upon their first meeting. Even when Johnny disproves Hot Pants's accusations, Hot Pants merely backs off and doesn't apologize for her attack, claiming that the duo was guilty of eating some of her meat anyway. This behavior earns her a particular enmity from Gyro's part, who would see her as an enemy.

Hot Pants speaks in a particularly rough and masculine manner despite her gender, for instance using the pronoun Ore (オレ) to refer to herself. This and her clothes allow her to pretend to be a man and perform her mission under an alias.

Hot Pants has a somewhat loose moral compass - she attacks, spares, and allies with potential competition at her leisure. For example, she heals Johnny and Gyro's life-threatening injuries after their fight with Sandman, but not before knocking Johnny out and taking his Corpse Parts. Hot Pants often frames her temporary partnerships as mutually beneficial deals, for example providing Lucy with a disguise and helping her in battle, while still enlisting the young girl as a personal spy, and swaying Diego toward working together by promising information that would help him take revenge on his father. However, she notably pays a few favors to Johnny Joestar, as the two seem to develop a quiet relationship of mutual respect despite their clashing goals - Johnny has kept her true identity and mission a secret from Gyro, while Hot Pants let Johnny keep his Stand by leaving a single vertebra from the Corpse Part after robbing him of the rest, and advised him to run away and leave both her and Gyro to die in their battle against Civil War.

Hot Pants harbors great guilt. As a child, she and her younger brother were attacked by a bear and Hot Pants ultimately pushed her brother toward the bear to escape. Having kept her dark secret from everyone, Hot Pants became a nun to seek forgiveness from God and her brother. She is dedicated to the search for the Saint's Corpse as she hopes that in gathering them, she will also be granted forgiveness from the Saint. For instance, she shows a rare bliss when taking a Corpse Part and is ready to risk her life against Funny Valentine. Despite being sent on the hunt for the Corpse Parts as a government agent of the Vatican, she seems to regard the search more as a path toward personal salvation.
Abilities: Stand
Hot Pants's Stand is Cream Starter; a handheld aerosol spray-like device, generating flesh as well as channeling her own; enabling her to distort and extend her body, and seal wounds.
Horseback Riding

Hot Pants is a skillful horseback rider and serious competitor in the Steel Ball Run race. Although she is not often seen riding, she has managed to always stay among the top racers in each of the stages she participated in (for instance ending at the sixth place during the 1st Stage), and she also won the 3rd Stage with a significant lead of one hour over the other top competitors.

personagens.resumo: Mountain Tim (マウンテン・ティム, Maunten Timu) is a secondary ally featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run. He is also the protagonist of the light novel Lonesome Tim.

ja_kanji.texto: マウンテン・ティム

namesake.texto: Mountain Jam (The Allman Brothers Band song)

cod.texto: Executed by gunshot to the head by Blackmore

voiceactor.texto: Joshua David King (English Dub) | Raphaël Cohen (French Dub) | Till Endemann (German Dub) | Ashish Tyagi (Hindi Dub) | Gianluca Crisafi (Italian Dub) | Thiago Zambrano (Brazilian Portuguese Dub) | Alejandro Orozco Antunez (Latin Spanish Dub) | Lluís Nicolau (European Spanish Dub) | Pavlo Skorokhod'ko (Ukrainian Dub)

Appearance: Mountain Tim is a man of average to above-average height, average build and has light hair. In the manga, his mullet is drawn to look permed while in the anime it has a much straighter texture. He later acquires a scar crossing his face.

He wears a stereotypical range of cowboy attire, consisting of a large hat, a wide-collared top exposing his upper chest, a neckerchief or a scarf, gloves, a belt with a gun holster on the right side, and boots with spurs. His hat has a zebra print with a miniature cow's skull as a decoration, while the clothing on his upper torso and his neckerchief have a leopard print; in the manga, his gun holster also has a leopard print. His belt buckle is round and bears his initials, "MT". Finally, he wears a sheriff's badge in the shape of a five-pointed star on his left side.
Color Schemes
Personality: Mountain Tim is confident and composed, with a strong sense of responsibility toward others. Sheriff Derek describes him as a well-liked cowboy with friends throughout the American West. Tim is unwilling to overlook the murders of his fellow competitors, explaining that many of the racers are his friends and that he cannot race with peace of mind while a murderer is among them.

Tim takes a practical, encouraging view of Stand abilities. He rejects the idea that his power is a curse, instead regarding it as a latent ability that enables him to confront danger. He willingly shares his knowledge with Johnny Joestar and Gyro Zeppeli, explaining the nature of Stands and warning them about the Devil's Palm.

Tim is openly romantic, falling in love with Lucy Steel at first sight despite her age and picking flowers for her with his lasso. He longs for someone who will welcome him home after his journeys and declares that even a smile from Lucy would make him willing to face hell. Although disappointed that she is married, he accepts her devotion to Steven Steel rather than pressuring her to return his feelings. His dialogue is altered in the anime; rather than being disappointed about Lucy being married, he claims that he is aware of her concern for her beloved husband due to the murders in the race and to leave it to him.

Tim's concern for Lucy outweighs his fear of death. He refuses to identify her to Blackmore, even when offered treatment for his wounds in exchange. He does not expect a peaceful death as a cowboy, but wishes for a place to return to after his travels.
In Lonesome Tim

As a teenager, Tim is proud of his talents and dismissive of those he considers less skilled. He values independence and the freedom to explore more than the security of a well-paid job. His confidence and unwillingness to compromise alienate his fellow soldiers, and he initially rejects Wyre's advice to respect their experience, insisting that his life and accomplishments are his own concern.

Wyre's principle of respect becomes central to Tim's outlook after his experience in the Devil's Palm. He comes to believe that people, animals, and the land deserve respect regardless of personal gain or differences in ability. He regards both the platoon's disaster and his own rescue as consequences of how they treated others, and credits his popularity as an adult to showing respect to everyone except criminals.

Although Tim enjoys the freedom of traveling, he acknowledges its dangers and loneliness, explaining that he has no place he can truly call home. He recognizes a similar loneliness in Standing Little Bear, who has lost her family, and encourages her to keep living in the hope of finding trustworthy people and a place to return to. His concern extends to small acts of kindness, such as giving her his only bedroll and covering her with a blanket.

Tim places Little Bear's safety above his pride and his own life. He refuses to accept Reed Whipman's challenge to a gunfight near her, insisting that protecting her takes priority over killing Reed. He also rejects the description of her as a cursed child and regards her ability as a blessing with which she can stand against fate.

Tim remains concerned for Johnny, Gyro, and Lucy after his retirement from the Steel Ball Run, and is relieved to learn that Johnny and Gyro are doing well in the race. He enjoys the quiet before sleep, music around the campfire, and black coffee made from his preferred beans.
Abilities: Stand

Mountain Tim's Stand, Oh! Lonesome Me, allows his lasso to separate his own body or another person's body it connects into pieces, move them along the rope, and reassemble them. This movement is restricted to the rope itself, limiting how far the separated parts can travel. Tim uses it to move his body while entangled with Johnny and Gyro, extend his reach through a vent to rescue Lucy, and move his gun-holding hand along his rope during his fight with Blackmore.

He first manifests the ability in 1875, at the age of sixteen, while serving with a cavalry reconnaissance unit in the Arizona desert. After the unit becomes lost in the Devil's Palm and the other soldiers die, Tim awakens to find parts of his body moving along his rope.
Equestrianism & Horseback Riding

Mountain Tim is an experienced cowboy who is introduced as traveling 4,000 kilometers through pasture each year with 3,000 cattle. His reputation makes him a favorite before the race begins. Riding Ghost Rider in the Sky, he finishes the first stage in fourth place and earns 35 points. Horses also lower their heads when he approaches, which Sheriff Derek describes as a sign of respect.
Lasso Handling

Tim handles his lasso with considerable precision. He can pick a flower while mounted on his horse and collect a bloodstained button as evidence, placing it into a glass bottle with the rope. He also uses it to restrain Benjamin Boomboom when the latter attacks him while disguised as Johnny.
Observation & Deduction

While investigating the murders, Tim examines hoofprints to assess the suspected killer's horse and route. He notices an unusual gait and distinguishes the culprit's tracks from those of Mrs. Robinson's horse by their horseshoe markings.

During his encounter with Oyecomova, Tim identifies the danger of removing the pins created by Boku no Rhythm wo Kiitekure. Despite his injuries, he warns Gyro that releasing a pin causes an explosion and deduces that a pin can be safely reinserted into its original hole, allowing Gyro to neutralize a bomb attached to his hand.
Abilities in Lonesome Tim

Tim uses Oh! Lonesome Me in a variety of ways. He secretly removes a cheating gambler's revolver and avoids a knife strike by separating his hand, then uses the detached hand to seize the man's face. Against two robbers, he moves his gun-holding hand behind them along a rope and shoots their hands to disarm them. He can also continue speaking through a detached mouth: leaving it behind to distract Reed Whipman, he moves the rest of his body away and uses a separated arm to carry Little Bear out of danger.

Tim is skilled with a revolver, having practiced regularly since his youth. At sixteen, he hits a cactus approximately forty meters away while mounted, although his first shot misses. His experience sleeping outdoors also makes him sensitive to faint sounds; he wakes at the approach of Reed and his companion and uses their footsteps to judge their direction and intentions.

He has practical camping skills, preparing a campfire, a stew of beans, bacon, onions, and herbs, and coffee for Little Bear. He attributes his cooking to copying the cook who accompanies his cattle drives.

personagens.resumo: Funny Valentine (ファニー・ヴァレンタイン, Fanī Varentain) is the main antagonist of the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, as well as the sixth main antagonist of the series overall.

occupation.texto: The 23rd President of the United States

goals.texto: Establish the United States as Earth's dominant superpower | All the rights and power to shape the future, leaving his name in history[b]

family.texto: Unnamed father | Unnamed mother | Dogs (Pets) | Captain Valentine (Stepfather) | Scarlet Valentine (Wife)See: Valentine Family

cod.texto: Fatally shot by Johnny Joestar

voiceactor.texto: Jason Marnocha (English Dub) | Dimitri Winter (Italian Dub) | Nestor Chiesse (Brazilian Portuguese Dub) | Valentino Tiron (Romanian Dub) | Jorge Badillo (Latin Spanish Dub)

Appearance: Throughout the narrative, Valentine adopts two main appearances, differing greatly in build. He is originally introduced as an old, stout, overweight man. Around the time he takes the rib cage of the Saint's Corpse, he gains a more fit and muscular appearance.
Valentine bears deep scars spanning his back, in a pattern resembling that of the 21st-century flag of the United States.

He has long, light hair, curling at its ends into several thick, well-defined rings (perhaps as a reference to the white periwigs and hairstyles of the 18th century, as worn by several early United States Presidents).

He also normally dons a smooth, uniform outfit, including an overcoat close to the end of his torso. Under this he wears a frilled sleeveless form-fitting shirt and a pair of gloves with a net pattern on the upper half.
Color Schemes
Personality: Valentine's foremost characteristics is his deeply patriotic ultranationalism for America. Marked by the gruesome fate of his father, Valentine's goal is for the United States to stand over the rest of the world. To do so, he seeks the blessing of the Saint Corpse Parts, becoming ecstatic when the Corpse blesses him. Moreover, the President shows a great degree of determination toward this goal. First acting through his subordinates early on in Steel Ball Run, Valentine later takes a greater active part in seizing the Saint's Corpse himself, confronting his enemies personally if need be, and claiming that he has no problem putting his life on the line to fulfill his objectives. He notably manages to regain his composure even after facing the eternal torture that Tusk ACT4 had inflicted upon him, dying many times, but always transferring his Stand to the next alternate Valentine. This is fueled by one of his expressed fears being to have someone petty or worse seizing the Corpse and taking away the happiness that he believes should go into the United States.

Despite this, Valentine is also callous about the lives of individual Americans, never hesitating to sacrifice his subordinates in his quest for the Corpse and going as far as to kill them himself if he deems it necessary. An example of this is how he cruelly traps an innocent train engineer halfway through a mirror just to assure himself of one advantage. His patriotism also comes with some hypocritical egotism. Despite his declared goal of working for the interests of the country, he regularly declares that "his" goals are fulfilled, and after witnessing Love Train's ability, shouted that everything, including power and glory, was now "his" specifically. Notably, when he was infatuated with Lucy Steel, disguised as his wife, Valentine attempted to sexually assault her and declared that she would bear his child, saying that he wanted a dynasty to ensure the United States would remain at the top.

Valentine is a ruthless individual, having a might-makes-right attitude toward the world, constantly using the metaphor of "taking the napkin first" to signify his gain in power. He believes that power is founded on authority, and part of the reason he wants the Corpse is to obtain a spiritual authority on par with the Vatican. Convinced that not everyone's wishes can be fulfilled and one must always sacrifice something for the sake of another, Valentine chooses to put the United States' prerogatives above the interests of the rest of the world. Valentine respects ambition and ruthlessness and ultimately entrusts the Corpse to an alternate Diego Brando. On the other hand, he looks down on Steven Steel's less ambitious goals, calling his will superficial. Claiming that while his methods require the least sacrifices possible, they still liberally involve murder and general violence, as well as manipulation of the people around him.

In and out of combat, Valentine shows a careful and observant side, regularly watching and thinking about the situation to best evaluate his strengths and vulnerabilities. He made great care to disguise his search behind the Steel Ball Run race to leave rival countries behind, but also closely watched the race, following the racers inside a train and having underlings stand to among within the participants, possibly recruiting them afterward, hence the abundance of enemies that Johnny and Gyro face throughout their journey. Valentine also understandably keeps tabs on the whereabouts of the Corpse parts, which after killing Axl RO, allows him to deduce that the infiltrator who broke into his residence was still near him. His observant nature makes him see through Diego Brando's disguise when the latter tries to approach him, and suspect Gyro's determination in their clash that something is amiss, fully grasping (with the help of a lucky wind gust) the danger the Spin poses to him and how it works. However, in his final confrontation with Johnny, Valentine decides to take his chances against the Spin, conceitedly allowing Johnny a last "futile" attempt at shooting him.

Valentine also demonstrates a generally dignified and composed attitude. He is a polite man, among others using the formal and neutral pronoun "Watashi" (わたし) for himself, and rarely losing his composure enough to insult someone. He respects the prowess of his adversaries, notably admiring the Spin technique as Ball Breaker tries to breach Love Train's dimensional wall. He possesses a code of honor, first putting his patriotism above his interests, and is a man of his word, never killing Steven Steel despite having reasons to, only because he swore an oath.

This is, however, contradicted, as Valentine will twist his code in desperate situations, and isn't above lying to gain an advantage, notably feeding Johnny with false hopes and half-truths to persuade him into releasing him from Tusk ACT4's ability. He also isn't above some petty moments such as slamming one of his men into another dimension to get rid of him, or stomping Steven Steel's wounds to make him suffer as frivolous revenge for him slightly thwarting his plans. During his earlier appearances, Valentine emoted much more, slightly losing his cool on several occasions and also privately calling Diego a "peasant" for having the gall to negotiate with his person on the same level.

Funny Valentine is generally polite but cold toward any individual. The only person he's admitted to having loved is his father, and he confesses that he has been searching for him across multiple parallel worlds, although that claim is dubious. Although his family appears to be happy, their love is shallow.[b] Despite his marriage with Scarlet and the two sharing a certain fondness for each other, Valentine only appeared to be a little disturbed by her death. Valentine also keeps a professional distance from his subordinates at best, only caring that they fulfill his orders, whether they die or not.

Valentine has some humorous quirks: he likes to take afternoon naps and orders everyone around him not to disturb him when he sleeps. He also tends to sometimes exclaim "dojyan!" (ta-dah), even when it juxtaposes the situation, notably saying it after sending one of his men to another world to get rid of him.
Abilities: Stand
Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap

Valentine's Stand, Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap (D4C), enables him to access any number of parallel worlds at any time; where, if desired, he may transfer his Stand to a counterpart of his, granting him pseudo-immortality. This requires him to get caught between two objects (for example, a flag and the ground or a sofa and the wall). This limits D4C's ability but not by much since he has gotten caught between water and the bottom of the ocean as a method of using his ability before.
D4C Love Train

When Lucy develops Ticket to Ride, Valentine may utilize a protective wall of light emanating from her which deflects all misfortune, bolstering his defense further as he becomes effectively invincible. He names this complementary ability "D4C - Love Train".
Personal

Charisma: Valentine is an accomplished politician, and enjoyed a high enough popularity to become President. Valentine demonstrates his charisma when he's able to negotiate with Johnny Joestar and perform a great enough speech to convince the jockey that he has the moral high ground, all that with a short amount of time to prepare.

Instrumental Skills: According to his wife, he makes no sound when he walks, and he can even play the mandolin using his feet, simply by dancing on it. Aside from the mandolin, Valentine has displayed a talent in playing the violin. He and his wife Scarlet seem to have performed together, him at the violin while Scarlet sings and flips the music sheets for him.

Appearance: Sandman is a man of average to above-average height and athletic build. He wears his mostly light hair in two long braids crossing his face. On both side of his biceps is a tattoo of a slithering snake inside a circle, lined with triangles pointing inward, while on his right chest are three lines that resemble check marks.

Sandman wears minimal clothing, leaving several portions of his skin exposed. On his torso he wears a dark form-fitting corset that leaves his chest exposed; the trim of the corset is studded around the top portion and a series of studs also encircle his abdominal muscles. He also wears a loincloth with a blade sheath, armbands, and wristbands, as well as leg warmers trimmed at the top with a fringe that wrap his calves and partially cover his feet, leaving only his toes and heels exposed. These pieces of clothing were initially studded with small square tags but they do not appear throughout the story; in the anime, only his loincloth retains these studs. Finally, Sandman wears a fabric collar decorated with dark jagged patterns as a trim and a row of X-shaped symbols running along the middle of the cloth.
Color Schemes
Personality: Sandman is a Native American with a singular and cynical outlook on the world but who is also loyal to his people.

Sandman is introduced as an open-minded member of his community, for instance shown in the possession of books expressively forbidden by them due to originating from white settlers and having developed his unique and admittedly extraordinary running style while ignoring his people's own techniques. Sandman is critical of his community, highlighting to his sister their outdated views and their misconceptions. For instance he claims that the idea of a claim to an ancestral land is out-of-date when the majority of the population now thinks on a financial level. Nonetheless, he is ready to take the risk to participate in a continent-spanning horse race to give back stolen lands to them, showing a great degree of loyalty.

Despite his open-mindedness, Sandman still treats the "white man" fundamentally as an enemy and sustains the idea that their society is governed by money. He ultimately sides with Funny Valentine, working to take the Corpse Parts to negotiate the necessary money to buy back his ancestors' lands. Disinterested in the corpse and the stakes at play, Sandman only considers it as a potential bargaining piece. When he confronts Johnny, Sandman also ultimately blames the white man's obsession for money as the reason of their current feud.

Sandman shows a great deal of determination and confidence. During his first appearance, he notably jumps under a running horse to purposefully be kicked high in the air and escape pursuit. Learning about the Steel Ball Run race, Sandman also decides without hesitation to leave his home to cross the United States on foot alone, expressing great confidence in his skill. However, his sister also points out that he is also solitary and stubborn to a fault since childhood, making it difficult for others to understand him. Sandman also doesn't shy away from committing questionable actions and readily fight Johnny and Gyro with the intent of killing them.

Sandman also shows a slightly honorable side. During the 1st Stage, he gives some of his time to tip Pocoloco and help him climb a cliff and, after he wins the first place in the 1st Stage due to a technicality, makes the effort to "repay" Gyro and warn him about an incoming storm. Finally, although he was ready to kill Johnny and Gyro, he is the only enemy to have taken the time to ask them for their Corpse Parts, even though he threatened them.
Sandman is very close to his sister. She is the only person with whom he shares his personal opinions and his final thoughts are to her, hoping for her happiness.
Abilities: Stand
Sandman's Stand, In a Silent Way, allows him to create three-dimensional constructs out of sounds.

Appearance: Pocoloco is a dark-skinned man of below-average to average height and slim or medium build. He sports a horseshoe mustache.

Throughout the race, Pocoloco wears a light, cropped tank top and pants, which sport a brick-like pattern. He is also seen wearing a harness, knee high boots, and a classic leather aviator helmet covered with distinctive elliptical pieces.
During the crossing of the frozen strait, he wears a long-sleeved shirt sporting a similar design as his tank top.
Color Schemes
Personality: Pocoloco is an optimistic, cheerful, and happy-go-lucky man who drifts through life at his own pace. He is not bitter over his poor background, but instead clings to a simple belief that his circumstances can turn around if fortune finally comes his way. Pocoloco's belief in luck is the core of his outlook. After being told his fortune will dramatically improve within the next two months, he becomes openly confident and acts as if his success is already guaranteed, talking himself up as an extraordinarily lucky man and interpreting events through that lens. Consequently, he lies on the ground and idly counts clouds, deciding he'll live an easy life rather than working. Pocoloco's optimism is not perfectly steady. When events initially go badly, he is quick to doubt himself and even questions whether the fortune teller's prediction was wrong, treating misfortune as proof that he is not actually lucky. However, his confidence rebounds just as quickly once something favorable happens, and he immediately reframes the situation as validation that he truly is a "one-in-five-billion" lucky guy.

Pocoloco's confidence can become reckless. Unlike other racers who rely on technical equestrian skills or their abilities, Pocoloco relies entirely on blind faith in his own luck. He takes dangerous risks with little hesitation, pushing forward as if nothing can hit him, and treating near-disasters as things that will simply work out. Once, he even takes the risk of his horse galloping full speed through a dense forest with his eyes closed. His decisions are usually improvised or instinctive rather than planned, with other racers like Johnny Joestar and Gyro Zeppeli viewing his behavior as irrational or impossibly fortunate. This attitude is reinforced by his Stand Hey Ya!, whose guidance functions as constant emotional reassurance. Pocoloco initially treats the experience as a hallucination, but he still listens closely to the Stand's upbeat directions and encouragement, letting it steer his choices and keep his confidence intact under pressure. In later stages, he continues to rely on that same upbeat momentum, persevering to stay in the lead. He is also competitive, goading Gyro by calling him an old man and declaring that once he takes the lead, Gyro will never take it back from him.

Pocoloco often yells out "Yo!". He also frequently exclaims joyful variations of "UH OH" when he experiences good luck. This is changed to "OH YEAH" or "Yeah, baby!" in VIZ Media's English publication.
Abilities: Stand
Hey Ya! is a Stand that cheers Pocoloco on and serves as a guide for him, taking full advantage of its user's absurd amount of luck.
Horseback Riding

Pocoloco is a competent horse rider who, thanks to his luck, becomes a serious competitor in the Steel Ball Run race. During his first appearance, Pocoloco shows an affinity with horses when he is able to guess that a mare is pregnant and at which stage her pregnancy is just by looking at her droppings. While he doesn't have the raw talent or the special skills of other top competitors, Pocoloco has tremendous luck and an absolute confidence, in no small part thanks to Hey Ya!. This gives him the possibility to boldly overcome obstacles in his way and stay a serious competitor throughout the entirety of the race. For instance, he was able to cross a forest by sheer luck and with his eyes closed (which incidentally allowed his horse to navigate through the forest by itself) whereas several other competitors crashed against the branches and fell.

Appearance: Benjamin is a middle-aged man of average to above-average height and a muscular build. His most peculiar feature is the metallic apparatus covering his lower jaw, which he can sink inside his face to change his facial structure. Benjamin also sports a bowl cut and a stubble, and he has no eyebrows.
His outfit consists of a long, dotted cloak with a target imprinted on it, a pair of pants with dark rings around each leg, and a belt around his waist.
Color Schemes
Personality: Benjamin is ruthless and greedy, seeking to secure the race's prize money for his family by eliminating competitors. He dismisses the warnings surrounding the Devil's Palm, claiming that the powers his family acquired there brought them happiness rather than misfortune.

He is verbally abusive toward his sons, particularly L.A., whom he insults even when L.A. points out practical problems with their plans. He also disparages his absent wife when comparing L.A. to her. His treatment of his children is inconsistent: he praises Andre as the family's most talented member and protects L.A. from gunfire. However, he dismisses Andre's fear of dying, shoots through the hole in his abdomen in an attempt to stop Gyro and Johnny, and ignores his worsening condition.

Benjamin takes pleasure in his victims' suffering, speculating about how far their organs will scatter and celebrating his family's good fortune while preparing to kill them. Despite his confidence, he warns L.A. to remain cautious until their enemies are dead, recognizing that a dying opponent may make a desperate final attack.
Abilities: Stand

Tomb of the Boom 1 gives Benjamin control over iron through magnetism. The Boomboom family can expose targets to its effect through blood or physical contact, causing affected people and iron objects to be drawn together.

Differently from his two sons, Benjamin shows much more prowess with his shared Stand. He is capable of moving the iron bracing he wears on his jaw into his skin to reshape his face, impersonating Johnny and using its sharp ends to cut Mountain Tim's rope. He is also able to grind down an incoming Steel Ball to a tiny marble before it can reach him, while also using his Stand to shield L.A. from bullets.

He wears a long-sleeved dotted shirt with a target imprinted on the chest. He wears a vest, cargo shorts, dotted pants, and a belt that he uses to asphyxiate himself.

He resents Johnny and Gyro for hesitating to help him after his venomous bite, even though he approached them as part of an ambush. Once the deception is exposed, he threatens to tear out Gyro's organs. Andre also laughs with his father at their enemies' predicament despite his own severe injury.

Andre practices erotic asphyxiation, claiming that he habitually lets women strangle him and has invented his own method of anesthesia through self-strangulation. He boasts about the experience while warning Johnny and Gyro not to imitate it. Andre acts tough at first, but becomes frightened as his wound worsens. He tells Benjamin that he might die and asks for help when he begins to feel cold and his vision blurs.

Benjamin states that Andre is the most talented in the family. Tomb of the Boom 2 gives Andre control over iron through magnetism. Contact with his blood can expose another person to the family's magnetic effect, causing metal to gather on their body and drawing affected targets together. Benjamin exploits this by shooting through Andre's wound to splash blood onto Johnny.

Appearance: L.A. is a young man of below-average to average height with long, voluminous hair and a notably feminine face. L.A. has thin eyebrows, sometimes inconsistently shown as no eyebrows in the manga. He wears goggles at the top of his head. His outfit is a long-sleeved collared shirt and pants similar to his father's. The shirt has a target imprinted on the chest and dots covering the surface, and the pants have dark rings around each leg. L.A. also wears a belt around his waist.

Personality: L.A. is childish, naive, and prone to emotional outbursts. He struggles with basic arithmetic, asking his family to calculate the combined prize money for finishing in the first three places. He also believes Andre's claim that their mother was a stork and wonders if he looks like one.

He is emotionally dependent on his father and brother and looks up to Andre, admiring his tricks and asking how he performs them. Despite their frequent insults, L.A. remains attached to both. He cries when he thinks Andre has died, embraces Benjamin while expressing how fortunate he feels, and becomes furious when Johnny kills his father.

L.A. occasionally makes useful observations, only to be mocked by his family. When he points out that Gyro and Johnny are beyond the range of Benjamin's bullets, Benjamin calls him a "know-it-all". He also questions how they will catch up to the pair when they are already among the leading racers, prompting Benjamin to sarcastically call him "the family's smart-ass".

L.A. also shares his family's cruelty. He eagerly asks to approach their victims so that he can watch their organs burst out, and tries to kill Johnny by drawing blood from his arteries. Even after his defeat, he continues threatening Johnny and Gyro.

Tomb of the Boom 3 gives L.A. control over iron through magnetism. He manipulates iron sand to bind his victims and prevent them from escaping. He also attempts to kill Johnny by drawing blood from his arteries, an attack Johnny interrupts with his spinning nails.

Appearance: Oyecomova is a man with long, thick locks of hair, several of which curl into spirals above his head. His face bears stars and striped markings resembling the American flag, while clock-face tattoos and curving patterns cover his arms and legs. When Mountain Tim grabs his shoulder, a layer of Oyecomova's skin peels away, exposing a darker layer underneath.

He wears a peaked cap decorated with a chain and openings through which his spiral-shaped hair protrudes. His outfit includes a sleeveless, high-collared vest fastened across a ribbed front panel, a skirt divided into long, pointed sections, wristbands, gloves, and high boots. A mesh veil covers his face. According to Hirohiko Araki, the netting protects him from sunlight and insects, reflecting practical preparation for the race.
Color Schemes
Personality: Oyecomova is composed and defiant when threatened. He continues searching Gyro's belongings while Mountain Tim holds him at gunpoint, answering Tim's questions with questions of his own. His warnings about touching him are delivered with the same composure: after Tim tears off a piece of his skin, Oyecomova tells him to keep holding it while calmly moving away from the impending explosion.

Oyecomova displays some semblance of religious spirituality as he regards his Stand as a divine gift and his survival in the Arizona Desert as God's will, interpreting his new ability as a mission entrusted to him. This conviction makes him boastful about his power. After discovering that Gyro's sweat will dislodge the bomb pins, he declares that God's handiwork has no weakness. Later, he compares Johnny and Gyro to mice trapped in a basket being put into a fire and boasts that his ability leaves them unable even to breathe.

Oyecomova is ruthless toward servants of the Neapolitan monarchy. He declares that he will not allow someone to race for the king, and taunts Gyro about his father's reported retirement, arguing that Gregorio bears responsibility for the prison guard Oyecomova killed during his escape. His hostility extends beyond Gyro, as he intends to return home and use his Stand to assassinate the king.

Despite his confidence, Oyecomova pays attention to his opponents' abilities. After Gyro wounds him, he estimates the range of the Steel Balls, considers whether the surrounding terrain favors him, and tries to remain just beyond throwing distance. He also anticipates that Johnny and Gyro might turn his explosive insects against him, although he fails to recognize the real purpose of their final attack until it is too late.
Abilities: Stand

Boku no Rhythm wo Kiitekure allows Oyecomova to turn things he touches into bombs fitted with clock-shaped detonators and removable pins. Once a pin comes loose, the bomb explodes after a short delay; keeping the pin in place prevents detonation. Mountain Tim discovers that a dislodged pin can also be put back into its original hole to stop the explosion.
Oyecomova applies the ability to his own shed skin, a rat, water, flying insects, and cigarette smoke. His use of smoke allows him to injure Gyro through the air he breathes.
Explosive Expertise

Before acquiring a Stand, Oyecomova used conventional explosives to bomb the Neapolitan king's carriage. While imprisoned, he killed a guard by putting a small amount of explosive in the guard's ear, allowing him to escape.
Combat Tactics

Oyecomova exploits the conditions needed to keep his bombs from detonating. He touches Gyro's hand to force him to hold his Steel Ball in place, then attacks with an explosive rat while Gyro is unable to throw it safely.

During the mounted pursuit, he uses the current to send water bombs toward his pursuers and disperses further bombs through wasps and smoke, attacking through the surrounding environment while staying ahead of them.
Horseback Riding

Oyecomova rides an unnamed horse and carries saddlecloth number 242. He reaches the 2nd Stage's intermediate checkpoint fourth, behind Mountain Tim, Gyro, and Johnny, although the checkpoint awards no points. He also maintains his lead over Gyro and Johnny while riding through a river and deploying his Stand.

Appearance: Pork Pie Hat Kid is a short, slender boy with a broad, angular jaw, prominent teeth, and large black irises. Upright bamboo sticks tied around his head conceal his bald scalp.

He wears a sleeveless, close-fitting outfit with an open, laced back. It is decorated with rows of circular studs along the chest and legs, short feathers at the shoulders, and a short, pleated skirt around the waist. His large wrist cuffs are decorated with leaves, and his boots have pointed toes.
The winch of Wired sits inside his mouth, while two hook-shaped recesses in his tongue accommodate its hooks.
Color Schemes
Personality: Pork Pie Hat Kid is eccentric and has unusual eating habits. While searching his targets' belongings, he drinks the ink from a broken pen and chews the pen itself, finding it delicious. After Johnny Joestar breaks three of his teeth, he wonders whether teeth taste good and if he can eat them. He also searches a bag by repeatedly hitting it with a rock rather than opening it normally.

His speech is similarly peculiar, as he repeatedly mispronounces Johnny's name and makes the mechanical-sounding cry "Gwee-Gachang (ギイイーガシャン, Gī Gashan)". He is eager for recognition and advancement. After obtaining the Saint's Corpse's left arm, he boasts that he has proved himself "invincible and smart" and will finally be acknowledged by others and rise in rank.

Despite his behavior, Pork Pie Hat Kid carefully considers his opponents' actions and adapts his tactics. When Johnny hides from him, he releases Slow Dancer to exploit the horse's instinct to return to its rider, then sets the surrounding ground on fire to force Johnny into the open. He also anticipates that Johnny will try to rescue Gyro, deliberately keeping Gyro alive to use him as bait.

He also finds his opponents entertaining despite the injuries they inflict. After Johnny's counterattack breaks three of his teeth, he calls Johnny and Gyro "an interesting pair" upon realizing that Gyro has sent a Steel Ball through his dish to help Johnny.
He is cruel and deceitful, threatening to tear Johnny apart while pursuing him. Although he agrees to spare Gyro in exchange for the Corpse Part, he intends to kill both men once he has it.
Abilities: Stand

Pork Pie Hat Kid's Stand, Wired, consists of a winch and two hooked cables inside his mouth. By lowering the hooks into a dish of water, he can send them to distant locations and reel in his targets. He uses feathers and insects as bait from which the hooks emerge, and can also make a person serve as bait.

personagens.resumo: Dr. Ferdinand (フェルディナンド博士, Ferudinando-hakase) is a secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, specifically the "Scary Monsters" story arc.

Appearance: Dr. Ferdinand is a man with light hair, that is parted with long bangs on the right side of his face. Most of his head is hidden under a thick hood.

His outfit's most notable feature is the several roses near the top of his long main garment, which appears to be only slightly shorter than his coat and resembles a dress or tunic. He dons a long, hooded coat, gloves, kneepads, pants, and boots.
He looks somewhat androgynous and seems to be wearing mascara - particularly below his eyes - and lipstick.
Color Schemes
Personality: Dr. Ferdinand is a geologist and a paleontologist with a very flamboyant personality. For him, the most important thing in the world is respect; he has a great respect for the planet, to the point he'd get senselessly furious should he see somebody spitting on the ground or littering. He's convinced that Earth brings prosperity only to those who respect the soil and has come to believe that dinosaurs, the once undisputed rulers of the world, died because their small brains couldn't understand this basic ideal.

Dr. Ferdinand is also the first Steel Ball Run antagonist to be truly devoted to Funny Valentine, and not just a mercenary. He tries to obtain the Saint's Corpse, as he believes the completed body would bring not only respect and prosperity to whoever obtains all the pieces, but true power and an eternal kingdom. He plans to recover them for the President, the only one who can actually exploit this power for the glory of a nation.
Abilities: Stand
Ferdinand uses Scary Monsters to turn Diego Brando into a dinosaur and have him affect an entire village. By directing orders to Diego, he is able to command an army of dinosaurs to do his bidding.
