namesake.texto: Ringo Starr (Former Beatles drummer) | On the Road Again (Willie Nelson song)

goals.texto: Ascend to new spiritual heights and enter the "world of man" by dueling

family.texto: Unnamed father | Unnamed mother | Unnamed sisters

cod.texto: Fatal injuries via Spin energy

seiyuu.texto: Hiroki Yasumoto (All-Star Battle / Eyes of Heaven)

Appearance: Ringo is a man of average to above-average height and slim to average build. He has light hair passing his forehead, swept to his left; a long, thin mustache, a soul patch in the shape of a cartoonish skull, and a beard of two slim patches bordering his chin.

He wears a light cap-sleeved jacket with a tall collar, dark gloves revealing his thumbs and index fingers, and a wristwatch of a fine, modern design on his right. It's shown that his pants are lightly frilled and studded near the bottom of the legs.
As a gunman, Ringo also wields a gun with an assorted ammunition belt and holster. The gun is identified by Gyro as an 1874 Colt.
Color Schemes
Personality: Ringo Roadagain is a peculiar gunman fixated on duels.

When he was a child, Ringo was of particularly weak constitution, as he easily bled and fell ill frequently. When a deserter killed his family and threatened to kill him, Ringo awakened his fighting spirit and shot the man dead to defend himself. At this point, Ringo ceased to be afflicted with illness and it shaped his entire mindset.

As of his introduction, Ringo is obsessed with bettering himself through duels. Considering himself "incomplete", he wants to reach new spiritual heights through duels, thinking that the pure killing intent he experiences elevates his spirit. Because of this, he also has a strong personal moral code: Ringo prefers to fight on completely fair grounds and will even give pointers to his opponents regarding their weapons and position to perfectly level the playing field before their battle begins. Able to discern the dark will to kill in people, Ringo prefers to duel people who won't hesitate to kill on the spot so that his duels are as tense and pure as possible. For instance, Ringo initially refused to fight Gyro and preferred Johnny whom he saw had the will to kill him.

Accustomed to risking his life in duels, Ringo shows a remarkable ability to keep his calm in the face of danger, not panicking even when the unexpected happens or when being outnumbered. On the other hand, he also readily acknowledges his nervousness when anticipating duels when Gaucho points out his shaking hand. He is also able to recognize an opponent's ability and cunning, praising how Gyro outsmarted him.

Ringo makes a point in differentiating between societal values and a man's values, believing that one finds his true strength in discovering the latter and that he will walk the "path of light" and live in "the world of man" once he does. He thus looked down on Gyro as a "conformist", in that he was chained down by the religious dogma forced on him by his father. Then noticing Gyro's growing determination, Ringo tried to steer him toward his own self-centered philosophy, telling him to go toward a "path of light" to victory.

In general, Ringo speaks gravely, acts with finality, and is usually extremely polite to those around him, even his foes. For instance, he makes it a point to bow when meeting someone and after defeating them, solemnly thanking them for the duel.
Abilities: Stand
Ringo's Stand, Mandom, enables him to reverse time by exactly 6 seconds by turning a hand on his wristwatch. Although it is very limited, its ability is critical for Ringo to win his duels.
Gunslinging
Ringo is also a capable gunfighter and seems to have incredible perception regarding gauging the range of various guns. He utilizes an 1874 Colt during his battle with Gyro Zeppeli.

personagens.resumo: Blackmore (ブラックモア, Burakkumoa) is a secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, introduced in the "The Green Tomb" story arc.

ja_kanji.texto: ブラックモア

cod.texto: Succumbed to multiple gunshot wounds inflicted by Lucy Steel

Appearance: Blackmore is a man of average to above-average height and medium build.

He wears a black, hooded poncho, punctuated in two columns on its chest, and lining its sleeves by small metallic rings. Through the top of its hood is threaded a long ponytail of his light hair. Underneath, he wears light clothes covering his arms to his metacarpals; and his pants and boots in a piece, patterned by a design resembling a paisley or a halved taijitu symbol.
Color Schemes
Personality: Blackmore is an efficient assassin, deeply loyal to Valentine; equally believing in his authority and cause.

Blackmore is largely depicted with a placid personality, talking slowly and being impassive to most things. However, his mission towards the Corpse Parts excites himself greatly and he even becomes exalted when he feels the presence of Jesus Christ.
Usually obedient to Valentine, he falls to a brief temptation to take the Corpse for himself but regains his senses after being shot, ultimately deeming that Valentine is the worthiest of them all.

Alongside Blackmore's calm personality is his great analytical acumen, allowing him to effortlessly track an intruder and unmask Lucy Steel through the various indirect clues found during his short investigation. As one of the President's men, he also coldly approaches murder, killing Mountain Tim without a second thought and being prepared to do the same to Lucy, Gyro, and Johnny.

Blackmore has a notable verbal tic, as he regularly mutters "'Scuse me" (すいませェん, Suimasēn) to people, an informal derivative of "Excuse me" (済みません, Sumimasen). He keeps the habit even with his employer and current President, Funny Valentine.
Abilities: Stand

Blackmore's Stand, Catch the Rainbow, allows him to manipulate rain. He can halt falling drops, make them into threatening obstacles or a path for him to walk on in the air, and relocate parts of his body by melding with the rain.

personagens.resumo: Sugar Mountain (シュガー・マウンテン, Shugā Maunten) is the title of a secondary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, introduced in the "The Promised Land: Sugar Mountain" story arc. An old woman with the appearance of a young girl, she is trapped by and made the current guardian to a Great Tree possessing a Stand of the same name.

ja_kanji.texto: シュガー・マウンテン

family.texto: Unnamed Parents

Appearance: Sugar Mountain has the appearance of a young girl, with dark hair in a hime cut and straight, eyebrow-level bangs. She wears a bonnet, a necklace in the shape of a cluster of grapes, a short dark dress with a light one underneath, leopard-patterned sleeves, and long socks with a pair of leather boots.
Color Schemes
Personality: Behaving much like a young child with a vivid imagination, Sugar Mountain does not seem to have aged physically or mentally during the roughly fifty years she spent bound to the Tree. She passes her time playing make-believe with dolls made from cloth and twigs, and has drawn rooms for an entire 'house' within the tree-hollow she lives in. Johnny deduces that she is nearly blind, noticing the mark of a cane around her abode. In spite of her childish mannerisms, she highly values honesty, and is able to comport herself with some maturity when she explains the Tree and the nature of its Stand to Johnny and Gyro, making sure that they understand that they must use up all of the items given by the spring by sunset. She expresses a strong desire to free her parents and leave the forest with them together, and holds Johnny and Gyro in high regard for their ability to escape the Tree's ability.

personagens.resumo: The Great Tree of Sugar Mountain (シュガーマウンテンの大木, Shugā Maunten no Taiboku) is a giant tree located south of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run. It serves as a Devil's Palm, where the Saint's Corpse's ears and right arm can be obtained. It is introduced in the "The Promised Land: Sugar Mountain" story arc.

ja_kanji.texto: シュガーマウンテンの大木

Appearance: Noted to be over a thousand years old, the Great Tree of Sugar Mountain is a massive tree with several babbling springs nestled amidst its sprawling roots. Embedded within its trunk are the unfortunate souls ensnared by its Stand, with their faces usually contorted in anguish. The tree holds chamber adorned with etchings of horses and oxen skulls on the walls. Within this chamber, the current guardian drew a make-shift floor plan to emulate a home for a family.
Color Schemes
Abilities: Stand

The Stand attaches itself to the great tree and functions as a trial for those who discover the tree and its current guardian. Although seemingly easy to pass, the test becomes more difficult as it goes on and will push a person's will to its limits.

personagens.resumo: The Eleven Men (１１人の男たち, Jūichi-nin no Otoko-tachi) are a group of unnamed secondary antagonists featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, specifically in the "The Promised Land: Sugar Mountain" story arc.

Appearance: All eleven men share similar outfits consisting of a flat brim cowboy hat, a range coat, and a belt with a holster for their gun. Most of them have a pattern featuring small writing spread all over their hair and facial hair like a newspaper or a book.

Personality: Not much is known about their personalities beyond stoicism, but they have an uncanny ability to act in unison. They are also ruthless murderers, patiently hunting after Gyro and Johnny then during their fight, and exploit any setback thrown to them, using their comrades' corpses as shields and hiding spots for surprise attacks. Despite their ruthlessness, they seem to have a sense of honor, as they don't go out of their way to kill anyone but Johnny and Gyro, and the only surviving gunman left Johnny alone after acquiring the Corpse Part from him.

Araki suggests that each of the men are labelled in a cardinal manner as Tatoo 1 (タトゥー1(ワン), Tatū Wan), Tatoo 2 (タトゥー2(ツー), Tatū Tsu), and so on. It's also assumed that one among the undecet is the leader, but nobody knows who it is.

All Eleven Men share the same Stand ability, named TATOO YOU! It allows them to use each other's bodies as portals, letting them merge with each other and displace themselves.

personagens.resumo: Mike O. (マイク・O, Maiku Ō) is a secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, specifically in the "Tubular Bells" story arc.

ja_kanji.texto: マイク・O

cod.texto: Ruptured lungs and exploded throat via Cream Starter

Appearance: Mike O. is a dark-skinned man of average to above-average height and medium build. His head is shaved save for a dark, curly patch on his crown; and centered on the edges of both eyes, extending to mid-forehead and covering his cheekbones, he has two light, swerving tattoos tapering at both ends into a spiral.
He wears a heavy overcoat of a thick collar and a sort of thick braid lining the length of his torso; a neatly folded scarf, and pants covered regularly by short spikes.
Color Schemes
Personality: Mike O. is a fairly serious servant loyal to Funny Valentine.

As a bodyguard, Mike O is dedicated to his job. After an infiltrator intercepted Ringo Roadagain's message in a presidential building, Mike O. leads an exhaustive investigation of the staff and their relatives, making over 1000 detailed files of all personnel. He takes his duty as a symbol of honor and considers any breach of a presidential building a stain on his honor as the president's bodyguard. Mike O. takes any threat to the President's safety with upmost priority, displaying distress after discovering that the First Lady Scarlet Valentine died and searching for the perpetrator after hearing gunshots. On the other hand, Mike O is ruthless toward those that threaten the President. Although originally planning to the capture and brutally torture Hot Pants and Lucy Steel, he swiftly attempts to kill the two as an execution after learning of Scarlet's death instead. Likewise, Mike O. requested that he could execute whoever stole Ringo's message.

His conduct of his investigation and his dedication to his position as a bodyguard for the president make him both very thorough and patient, going to painstaking lengths to achieve his goals, going as far as to willingly rupture his lungs and throat in a last attack against Hot Pants with Tubular Bells.

Mike O. has a small habit where he repeatedly uses the word "world" (世界, sekai) in all its meanings. He complains by stating his body "is freezing up in this world", asks Diego Brando "how it's going in the world of racing" and theorizes that the person who infiltrates Valentine's government could "be involved in the world of Stand users".
Abilities: Stand

Mike O.'s Stand is Tubular Bells, which allows him to inflate metal akin to balloons and reshape it into living animals (dogs, swans, etc.). The balloon animals track and/or invade the body of a target, exploding and reverting suddenly to their metallic form.

personagens.resumo: Wekapipo (ウェカピポ) is a secondary antagonist, later a secondary ally, featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run. Introduced as an antagonist in the "Wrecking Ball" story arc, he then becomes an ally to Johnny Joestar and Gyro Zeppeli.

ja_kanji.texto: ウェカピポ

family.texto: Unnamed Sister | Unnamed Brother-in-Law

cod.texto: Obliterated after merging with his parallel world self

Appearance: Wekapipo is a tall man of athletic and somewhat muscular build. He is most notable for his bizarre haircut, sideburns, and beard, which consist of a series of shaved grid lines and squares of short hair. He enters the story sporting a mustache, which he later shaves off.

He wears a light-colored jacket covered with paired overlapping polka dots, which has an exaggerated cloak collar and feather-like protrusions in the back with a tie, and pants covered in the same design with a simialrly overlapped circular belt buckle. Like Gyro, his clothing also sports holsters for his Wrecking Balls, and he is also shown to have worn gloves when first introduced.
In the past, Wekapipo wore a much lighter-colored outfit with a cravat or ascot tie, which is inconsistently portrayed as being fastened with compact straps across the torso.
Color Schemes
Personality: Wekapipo is a remarkably stern and serious individual, focusing on whatever goal he has and tolerating little the hijinks of Magent Magent.

During his youth, Wekapipo was entirely devoted to his sister. He had gone out of his way to force a divorce after learning that her husband beat her. The news of her supposed death made him seemingly depressed and he has since then had a bleak outlook on life.

Wekapipo is a cold and somber man, constantly focusing on an objective and coldly working towards it. During a fight, he's been noted to pay attention to the strengths and weaknesses of his enemy and methodically suppress each of their advantages. Wekapipo does not tolerate his partner distracting him from their mission and repeatedly tells him to stop fooling around, be it chit-chatting or gloating in a fight. Having the sole ambition of obtaining a comfortable life, he wouldn't hesitate to betray Funny Valentine nor prepare to work against Gyro Zeppeli, aiming to join the winning side.

Wekapipo possesses an honorable side, being respectful of the prowess of the Zeppeli Family's Spin, and acts accordingly. Moreover, he agreed to temporarily help Gyro and Johnny after they revealed that the Zeppelis have been taking care of his sister. Upon being defeated, he tried to kill himself in order to escape the dishonor a loss would bring him before Valentine, although he implied that he would die for it at Valentine's hands nonetheless.
Abilities: Wrecking Ball
As a former royal guard member, Wekapipo possesses a unique type of steel ball that is normally wielded by the imperial guard serving the royal family.

personagens.resumo: Magent Magent (マジェント・マジェント, Majento Majento) is a recurring secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, introduced in the "Wrecking Ball" story arc.

Appearance: Magent Magent is a slender man of above-average height and dark curly hair. Outside a bolero hat, his attire generally consists of what appears to be a thick quilted stud jacket, accompanied by long sleeves, finger-less gloves, a fur collar, and a single stud-embedded cravat.
Later on, he is given a noticeable scar on the left side of his face after his bout with Johnny and Gyro.

Because his Stand is entirely defensive in nature, Magent Magent carries firearms with him. Against Johnny and Gyro, he wields a shotgun, was shown to use a pistol with a silencer for quiet assassinations, and was seen wearing an explosive belt.

Personality: Magent Magent is presented as an affable and genial henchman to Funny Valentine, trying to bond with his new partner Wekapipo through idle chat or questionable jokes. However, he is quickly exasperated by Wekapipo's gloomy attitude and comes to hate him for leaving him behind in the cold.

In contrast to Wekapipo's more dignified manners, Magent Magent has several bad habits such as licking his own snot, or is quick to express nervousness or frustration during his battles. His unprofessional behavior also causes him to botch most of his actions, such as when he wastes time taunting and threatening Wekapipo during their battle and allows the latter to counterattack and win.
Magent Magent supposedly has a nasal, gravelly and thus irritating voice. This is represented by his lines tending to be written phonetically rather than the more usual style.

He has a fondness for airplanes, marvelling at their potential for crossing great distances in a short time. After being left for dead in the frozen wilderness, he also complains that airplanes weren't invented earlier so that his wounds could be treated earlier.
Abilities: Stand
Magent Magent can summon 20th Century BOY in order to become invulnerable to all harm, including explosions and drowning, as long as he adopts a kneeling position and puts his hands on the ground.

personagens.resumo: Axl RO (アクセル・RO(ロー), Akuseru Rō) is a secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, specifically in the "Civil War" story arc.

ja_kanji.texto: アクセル・RO(ロー)

cod.texto: Shot by Johnny Joestar via Tusk (First death) | Fatal gunshot wound via Funny Valentine (Second death)

mangadebut.texto: SBR Chapter 56 (Voice only) | SBR Chapter 58 (1st full debut)

Appearance: Axl appears to be a middle-aged man of average to above-average height and medium build. Darkness (either shadow, paint or a tattoo) covers his face to just below his eyes and in mirrored, hook-like tribal marks on his cheeks; save for a scattering of dots.

Over a light, drooping rag, he wears a thick, round military helmet covered by a net. He wears a thick wide-necked top, bearing four dark rectangular patches between his shoulders and elbows on his long sleeves. His chest is overlaid with a V-shaped piece from which hang layers of squares; and he wears dark, knee-high boots.
Color Schemes
Personality: Axl's most characteristic trait is his desire to purify himself from his sins in order to rid himself of the ghosts of his past comrades haunting him.

When he was young, Axl aspired to become a musician like Antonín Dvořák but was enlisted to the army instead. After not being able to bear the terrors of war, he became addicted to alcohol. Axl prioritizes his own life above others. During the war, he had the opportunity to sacrifice his life to alert his companions of an incoming enemy troop, but chose to stay hidden and drink instead, letting the people of the nearby town be massacred.

With his Stand ability, he is able to abandon his sin and guilt by transferring it to somebody else. This is tied to his ideology that claims people have to sacrifice something in order to progress. Additionally, Axl believes that battles should be fair as stated when he told Gyro his Stand's weakness.

Most of the time Axl is shown to be composed, which was the case even back when he willingly sacrificed people for his own sake. He does however lose his temper and panic when Johnny risks damaging the Corpse, shouting and desperately trying to stab him.
Abilities: Stand

Axl's Stand is Civil War, constituting a system in which he is able to transfer or unload sin and guilt via the attacks of hostile, ghostly representations of people and objects he or his targets harbor as having wronged or unfairly discarded. Another part of Civil War's ability is that whenever he's killed and his killer feels even the slightest of guilt for killing him, he is brought back to life.

personagens.resumo: D-I-S-C-O (ディ・ス・コ, Di-su-ko) is a secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, specifically in the "Chocolate Disco" story arc.

ja_kanji.texto: ディ・ス・コ

He wears a long coat with several pockets in the front, as well as a belt connected with a handcuff-like accessory. Due to the nature of his Stand Chocolate Disco, he can be seen wearing the accessory like an armband on his left arm.
Color Schemes
Personality: D-I-S-C-O has a rather expressionless face and personality. He is very quiet and prefers to never speak more than is necessary, speaking only to reveal his Stand's name.

During battle, D-I-S-C-O is cautious around his enemies, preferring to keep his distance away from them while using his Stand to transport hazardous objects on wherever they would go. When cornered, however, D-I-S-C-O loses his composure and immediately relies on his gun, which Gyro mocks him for.
It is unknown what kind of relationship he might have with the President. Gyro Zeppeli believes him to know nothing about Valentine's plan.
Abilities: Stand
D-I-S-C-O's Stand is Chocolate Disco. It can create a grid he may project over a limited space in front of him wherein he maintains virtually complete control.

"Diego from a Parallel World"), commonly shortened to The World Diego (世界ディエゴ, Sekai Diego) or simply Dio(ディオ), is a secondary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

ja_kanji.texto: 並行世界から来たディエゴ | 世界ディエゴ

ja_romaji.texto: Heikō Sekai kara Kita Diego | Sekai Diego

namesake.texto: Diego Brando | Dio Brando (Parts 1 and 3 Antagonist) | Dio ("God" in Italian) | Ronnie James Dio (American musician) | Dio (American heavy metal band) | Marlon Brando (American actor)

cod.texto: Head obliterated after merging with his original world self's head

gamedebut.texto: All-Star Battle (Voice only) | Eyes of Heaven | (Playable)

Appearance: Parallel World Diego is virtually identical in appearance to the base world's Diego Brando. He is a young man of below-average height and slim to medium build. He has light hair, dark eyebrows, and light, bold eyes. He commonly wears an equestrian helmet with the letters "D", "I" and "O" mounted on bending pins emerging from a small ribbon tied at its front, a turtleneck jumper patterned with a diagonal grid, light, mid-forearm-length gloves, light, wide-legged breeches, and tall, dark riding boots.
Color Schemes
Personality: This incarnation of Diego Brando shares several personality traits with his base world counterpart: like the original Diego, he is misanthropic and ambitious above all, sharing his counterpart's desire for power and dominion over society. However, the methods by which he achieves his goals demonstrate far more overt cruelty and violent tendencies than the original Diego.

Parallel World Diego is self-centered and has no apparent capacity for empathy. When he first meets Valentine, he takes the president's final pleas lightly and in a joking manner until he is entrusted with the claim to the Saint's Corpse, quickly becoming interested only upon hearing about its power. Furthermore, he is absolutely ruthless, prepared to kill anyone in his way by inventively violent methods, including throwing knives, setting up wire traps, and even using gasoline and matches to burn others alive. He is capable of sacrificing innocent people without a second thought, going so far as to taunt Johnny for accidentally killing the adoring fans he uses to shield himself.

Due to his Stand's invincible power to stop time, Diego displays unshakable self-confidence and openly shows contempt for others. He only becomes distressed when he loses the upper hand or is shaken by an unexpected development, such as Tusk's ability to move within stopped time. When he is cornered by Lucy, he finally loses control of his emotions, screaming with rage and disgust his disbelief that the girl would dare to defy him.

Parallel World Diego also shows a tactical acumen, quickly noticing the danger of Tusk's infinite rotation and formulating a plan to do away with it while keeping his distance. Throughout his mission, he outsmarts Johnny time and time again, ultimately succeeding in inflicting the infinite rotation upon its own user.

He also notably has a predatory and lascivious side to him, which the original Diego Brando had never exhibited. Even while bleeding profusely from a dire injury, he forces himself on Lucy, choking and molesting the teenage girl while describing how he intends to thoroughly degrade her.
Abilities: Stand
Parallel World Diego's Stand, THE WORLD, is a powerful humanoid Stand capable of stopping time for up to five seconds.
Horseback Riding
The original Diego Brando is one of the most talented jockeys of his generation, and his alternate counterpart demonstrates the same level of expertise in riding and handling horses.

Appearance: Mrs. Robinson is a muscular and androgynous man with long, light-colored hair that fans outward into sharp points. He wears a dark head covering that leaves a crest of hair exposed along the top of his head. His face is characterized by dark lipstick and a large dark marking surrounding his left eye.

He wears an open, sleeveless vest decorated with numerous circular studs of varying sizes, leaving most of his chest exposed, along with striped arm coverings, loose pants, and boots. Numerous straps across his clothing and El Condor Pasa's tack bear the phrase "TRUE LOVE", potentially referencing Simon & Garfunkel's cover of Scarborough Fair. He also wears clusters of eyeballs attached by strings as earrings.
Robinson raises insects inside his body, with a large number of them shown emerging from his left eye socket when he reveals his technique.
Color Schemes
Personality: Mrs. Robinson is a ruthless and highly competitive participant in the Steel Ball Run. Rather than attempting to defeat other competitors solely through racing, he is willing to seriously injure or kill them to prevent them from getting ahead of him. After revealing the secret behind his attacks, he confidently declares that nobody in the race will be allowed to run ahead of him.

Having grown up in a village where disputes could escalate into fights to the death, Robinson developed his technique so that he would not be controlled by others and began raising insects inside his body so that he would never lose to anyone. This desire to remain undefeated is reflected in his determination to eliminate Johnny and Gyro during the race.

Robinson is confident in his technique and refers to its workings as his "secret." Once Gyro has been placed at a disadvantage, he openly explains how his insects control the surrounding chollas, but immediately intends to kill Gyro now that the method has been revealed. His confidence quickly turns to shock when Gyro discovers that the Spin can exploit the same property of the chollas and turn them against him.

He also fights cautiously, initially keeping his distance from Johnny and Gyro and attacking through the surrounding chollas without revealing how the needles are being launched. This allows him to attack from multiple directions while making it difficult for them to identify the source of the attack.
Abilities: Insect Manipulation

Mrs. Robinson raises numerous flying insects inside his body, with several shown emerging from his left eye socket. He uses the insects in conjunction with cholla cacti growing throughout the desert. Chollas are capable of releasing their needles in response to nearby disturbances and vibrations in the air. By directing his insects around his opponents, Robinson uses the high-speed pressure generated by their flight to trigger the surrounding chollas and send their needles toward specific targets.

The technique allows Robinson to attack from a considerable distance and from several directions at once. He demonstrates enough control to graze Gyro's ear, attack Johnny and Gyro from multiple sides, sever Johnny's reins, and repeatedly strike Johnny's face strongly enough to knock him from Slow Dancer. He is also able to target Gyro's arm while he attempts to use his Steel Balls, disrupting his throw.

Because Robinson himself does not need to approach the chollas he is activating, his opponents initially have difficulty understanding how the plants are being triggered. However, the technique can be turned against him because the chollas respond to other vibrations as well. Gyro eventually uses the vibrations produced by the Spin to trigger the plants surrounding Robinson.
Horseback Riding

Mrs. Robinson is a capable horse rider. Riding El Condor Pasa, he finishes the 1st Stage of the Steel Ball Run in 18th place and earns four points. During the 2nd Stage, he is able to follow Johnny and Gyro across the Arizona Desert for approximately six hours while maintaining a consistent distance behind them.

personagens.resumo: Luke (ルーク, Rūku) and Bishop (ビショップ, Bishoppu), also known as the President's Aides (大統領の側近, Daitōryō no Sokkin), are two tertiary antagonists featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

ja_kanji.texto: ルーク | ビショップ

Appearance: Luke and Bishop are middle-aged men with average builds. They wear identical uniforms and have curled hairstyles similar to Funny Valentine, though they differ in facial features, demeanor, and hairstyle arrangement. Their uniforms consist of an overcoat with a frilled shirt underneath.

Luke, the more assertive and vocal of the two, has a stern expression and long, light hair. His initial hairstyle features several large vertical rolls of hair framing the sides of his head, with a prominent central part, exactly like Valentine's hairstyle. He has a thin parted pencil mustache. In his first appearance, he also has a goatee, but it is gone in subsequent chapters. In his final appearance, his hairstyle changes to a longer, looser style, slicked back with the curls hanging below his shoulders instead of above them. His mustache has also grown longer, similar to the Fu Manchu style. His jacket is now closed, not revealing the shirt underneath.

Bishop also has long, light hair, though arranged differently. His hair is styled in a high topknot bun with long tails extending from it. His beard is styled as three vertical lines, with the line closer to his mouth pointing above his upper lip like a mustache. In his final appearance, the tails extending from his bun are a bit shorter and his beard no longer points toward his upper lip. His uniform has changed to be short-sleeved and he wears wristbands.

In the anime, their appearances have been altered slightly; Bishop now has slightly darker skin but otherwise matches his appearance with his final design whilst Luke moreso resembles his initial design but without the goatee like in subsequent chapters. In addition, unlike the manga where the two match the president's attire colour-wise, the two are depicted wearing similar but different shades.
Color Schemes
Personality: Luke and Bishop serve as loyal subordinates to Funny Valentine, acting as his direct enforcers, liaisons, and guards. Both aides are willing to carry out morally questionable orders without hesitation, whether it involves orchestrating Gyro Zeppeli and Johnny Joestar's assassinations or drugging Lucy Steel to keep her asleep while she is pregnant. Although the two are not stated to be Stand users, they are both aware of Stands, as Valentine tells them to summon Stand users.

Luke is authoritative, severe, and quick to issue threats. He conducts most of the President's logistical operations, responds to intelligence reports, and handles assignments such as negotiations or summoning assassins to pursue Johnny and Gyro. He frequently communicates with Valentine and acts as an advisor, offering calm and pragmatic responses when the President becomes frustrated or suspicious. When Valentine questions the failure of the hot air balloons and suspects Steven Steel of interference, Luke counters with rational explanations, emphasizing technical limitations of the balloons and the risks of destabilizing the race if they dispose of Steven. His composed and analytical nature helps temper Valentine's more impulsive decisions.

He does not hesitate to become hostile, as seen when he threatens Diego Brando with execution for overstepping his position. He is methodical and attempts to maintain control in chaotic situations, but his stoic façade begins to fray as Lucy's Stand causes successive injuries, particularly to his left eye. After Valentine orders them to make Lucy "docile like a winter catfish," Luke repeatedly echoes the phrase and demands that Bishop carry it out, which underscores his dependence on strict obedience and control.

In contrast, Bishop is quieter and more passive, only shown speaking to Luke. He appears more hesitant and cautious while they are watching over Steven and Lucy. Despite being the one to drug Lucy, he tries handling her carefully since she is pregnant. He is visibly disturbed by the inexplicable effects of Lucy's Stand, such as his repeated falls and Luke's consistent injuries.

personagens.resumo: Jesus Christ (イエス・キリスト, Iesu Kirisuto), usually referred to as The Saint (聖人, Seijin), is a secondary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

ja_kanji.texto: イエス・キリスト

namesake.texto: Jesus Christ (Jewish religious leader and central figure of Christianity)

cod.texto: Crucifixion (original death) | Unspecified (later death in America)

Appearance: Jesus has long hair and a slender body bearing numerous wounds and scars. His facial hair varies between depictions. He appears with a mustache and beard when first approaching Johnny Joestar, but is clean-shaven during another appearance in the same battle.

In the flashback of his resurrection and journey east, he wears a loose robe, with his face largely hidden by his hair or the garment. His appearances to Blackmore and Johnny show him wearing a crown of thorns. He also bears the Holy Wounds in his hands and feet.
Color Schemes
Personality: Jesus is quiet, composed, and enigmatic, often speaking only a few words. He expresses gratitude toward Joseph of Arimathea for caring for his body after his crucifixion. Rather than directly answering Joseph's tearful question about whether they will meet again, he draws a map and leaves him with a short statement about circles and rotation.

He is friendly and willing to learn from the people he meets. During his journey east, he lives among different communities and learns their languages and customs. People help him build a boat, and the inhabitants of the land where he spends the rest of his life express a wish to see him again.

His advice is solemn and often cryptic, leaving Johnny to discover its meaning for himself. He repeatedly tells Johnny not to shoot when his heart wavers and urges him to grow, promising that a new path will open to him.
Abilities: Divine Qualities

Jesus's presence can appear to people near the Corpse Parts. Blackmore sees him after taking the spine and describes the sensation as being enveloped in light. Johnny also perceives him as more than a hallucination, stating that he heard breathing and felt body heat behind him. The figure disappears when Johnny turns to look, but reappears to advise him during his fight with Axl RO.

Jesus returns to life three days after his crucifixion, despite wounds that should have made his survival impossible. He also appears to possess knowledge of future events, as the nine locations he marks on Joseph of Arimathea's Map correspond to the places where his remains are eventually scattered. His remains possess supernatural powers long after his death.
Saint's Corpse
Stand Abilities

Corpse Parts can merge with the corresponding parts of a living person's body, and acquiring one can awaken a Stand or another ability. The left arm, for example, enters Johnny's arm and grants him Tusk.
Equivalent Exchange

In JoJolion, the full Saint's Corpse is described as having the power of "removal," a phenomenon associated with Equivalent Exchange. It can remove an illness, but doing so may transfer the affliction to someone else. When Johnny uses it to cure Rina Higashikata, their son George Joestar III develops the Rock Disease instead.

Appearance: George Joestar is a mature man of average height who is slightly overweight. He has a double chin and several wrinkles. In the past, he has short, dark hair that is styled neatly, along with a mustache and long sideburns. His hairline is receding and the hair on the top of his head is combed to one side, creating a side parting. A single, wavy lock swoops down onto his forehead. Over time, his hair grays with age. In his final appearance, he has a visible widow's peak and no longer has the lock over his forehead or the side parting. Instead, his hair has a rounded, bushy appearance, sticking out on the sides. His face also has more wrinkles compared to before.

In his first appearance, George wore a dark top hat and suit. While having dinner with his family, he wears a dark single-breasted suit with notched lapels on top of a light dress shirt with a dark tie. When he's outside caring for Nicholas's horse, he wears sunglasses with small circle lenses. When arguing with Johnny about Nicholas's boots, his outfit consists of a dark vest over a light, collared dress shirt, and light pants. In his final appearance, George wears a dark duffel coat with horseshoe shaped accessories on top of a light turtleneck sweater.
Color Schemes
Personality: George is an acclaimed horse trainer. He is a strict father, not only forbidding a young Johnny from bringing an adopted mouse to the table while they're eating, but then ordering that the mouse is shown to him and then drowned. Since he is mindful of his reputation among the British, George is particularly severe when it comes to gentlemanly manners.

George shows favoritism toward his eldest son. Upon Nicholas's death, George becomes extremely sad and bitter. According to Johnny, George would spend the next seven years reminiscing about Nicholas's immense talents while downplaying Johnny's own achievements. He is adamant about not letting Johnny use Nicholas's riding boots, blaming Johnny for not taking care of his own boots. He also believes Johnny can't beat Diego Brando but that Nicholas could.

George ultimately changes his mind over time, regretting how he treated his son. Crying seeing how much Johnny has achieved, he meets with his son again in New York during the Final Stage of the Steel Ball Run, waving Nicholas's boots as a silent gesture of reconciliation. Finally, he publicly declares his shame over letting his son suffer and that he is proud of his achievement of having crossed the United States.

Over that bodysuit, Scarlet wears a short sleeveless dress with a multi-layered heart motif on the chest.

Scarlet follows her impulses when in a relationship. She is bisexual, as she shows affection towards her husband, but also desires intimate contact with women. One of her fetishes seems to be facesitting. She also prefers to be berated during sex according to her husband.

Scarlet's personality also has a violent side. As soon as she discovers Lucy Steel trying to infiltrate her husband's bedroom, Scarlet draws a gun without hesitation and tries to kill her, insulting her profusely as she shoots the girl. Moreover, Scarlet seems to become sadistic when pushed, as she declares that she will have Lucy tortured for daring to use her, and also stirs a nail driven in Lucy's leg to make her suffer.

personagens.resumo: She Who Dances with the Leaves (木の葉と踊る女, Konoha to Odoru Onna) in her tribe's native language,[b] often referred to simply as Sandman's Sister (サンドマンのお姉ちゃん, Sandoman no Onē-chan), is a tertiary character featured in the seventh part of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

Appearance: She Who Dances with the Leaves is a young woman of average height and build. She has dark, long hair with two light bangs hanging in front of her face. Her clothes are made of natural Native American materials such as wooden bangles and necklaces.
Color Schemes
Personality: She Who Dances with the Leaves is a traditionalist who strongly adheres to her peoples' values and beliefs. She disapproves of Sandman's interest in the white man's books and culture, seeing it as a betrayal of their community. She is strict and protective of her younger brother, scolding him and severely beating him for going against their customs.

She Who Dances with the Leaves is skeptical of white Americans and is quick to assume the worst when discovering an outsider’s tracks near the village. Much like other members of her community, she shares a narrow-minded perspective on her people's way of life and is resistant to change. Having grown up with Sandman, she wishes nothing more than for the two of them to peacefully return to the village; however, when Sandman reveals his plan to leave the village and win the Steel Ball Run race, she's taken aback. Nonetheless, she offers Sandman a keepsake from their parents to help him enter the race.
It's implied that, unlike her brother, She Who Dances with the Leaves is illiterate and unable to read.

personagens.resumo: Steven Steel's Secretary (スティーブン・スティールの秘書, Sutībun Sutīru no Hisho) is an unnamed tertiary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

Appearance: The secretary is an adult man of average height with defined cheekbones, a prominent nose and narrow eyes. He sports a mustache reaching down to the sides of his jaw. He has short hair which is slicked to the side.

Befitting his professionalism, his outfit consists of an ascot tie, shirt, vest and a patterned suit with a long jacket. While looking into the deaths of racers during the 1st Stage, he wears a patterned hat.
Color Schemes
Personality: The secretary shows himself to be professional from the surface, though somewhat underhanded in his methods. As the manager of the Steel Ball Run, he listens to complaints filed before reciting them to Steven Steel. He serves as Steven's voice of reason in the beginning of the race, informing him of budget problems and accidents. Despite this, he easily backs down and listens to Steven's orders. Acting from the shadows, he advises Steel to confront Gyro Zeppeli directly over his nationality after discovering Gyro's ties to European nobility.

Despite being the manager of the race, he is uninformed of Funny Valentine's goals and is not aware of the Saint's Corpse. After being ordered by Steven to investigate if Gyro is carrying the corpse, he expresses surprise about the sudden nature of the request and goes so far as to question Steven if the race has a hidden motivation, before being quickly dismissed.
After the Steel Ball Run Press Conference, the secretary also attempts to gesture away interviewers with inappropriate questions unrelated to the race.

personagens.resumo: Sheriff Derek (デレク保安官, Dereku Sherifu) is a tertiary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run, and a secondary ally in the light novel Lonesome Tim.

ja_kanji.texto: デレク保安官

namesake.texto: Derek and the Dominos (English–American Blues Rock Band)

Appearance: Derek is an older, heavyset man with a prominent belly. His most defining facial feature is a long, thick mustache that droops down well past his chin. He has long, curly hair falling past his neck.

Derek wears a wide-brimmed hat featuring a large shield-shaped badge reading "SHERIFF" pinned to the front crown. His typical attire consists of a patterned vest on top of a long-sleeved shirt, riding chaps, and a necktie, with a standard US Marshal star badge pinned to his left breast. He also has shield-shaped sheriff badges on his shoulders, wears a gun belt, and carries a rifle.
Color Schemes
Personality: Derek is a highly professional, observant, and fair lawman who adheres strictly to the laws and unwritten codes of the American West. Despite the brutal nature of his job, he maintains a level head. When Gyro Zeppeli uses the Spin to make a pickpocket shoot himself, Derek calmly assesses the situation and lets Gyro go, declaring that since both parties agreed to a fair duel, no laws were actually broken. He is also highly pragmatic and protective of the public peace; when discovering a gruesome mass murder during the race, he deliberately keeps newspapermen away from the crime scene to prevent a mass panic.
He holds immense respect for Mountain Tim, frequently relying on the cowboy's skills to apprehend criminals who have bounties.

In the light novel Lonesome Tim, Derek trusts Tim's character unconditionally, willingly deputizing him to act as an agent of the law to apprehend dangerous criminals like Reed Whipman and Clem Brown. Derek is shown to be highly amicable and easily swayed by Tim's philosophy of "respect," though Tim jokes that Derek is a lightweight drinker who will likely forget their conversations once he gets drunk.

personagens.resumo: Gregorio Zeppeli (グレゴリオ・ツェペリ, Guregorio Tseperi) is a tertiary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

ja_kanji.texto: グレゴリオ・ツェペリ

family.texto: Unnamed Wife | Gyro Zeppeli (Eldest Son) | Four Unnamed ChildrenSee: Zeppeli Family

voiceactor.texto: Keythe Farley (English Dub) | José García Tos (European Spanish Dub) | Dan Apăvăloaie (Romanian Dub) | Fabrizio Odetto (Italian Dub) | Laurent Maurel (French Dub) | Krishna Upadhyay (Hindi Dub) | Felipe Grinnan (Brazilian Portuguese Dub)

Appearance: Gregorio is a mature man with a lined face, short hair styled into a flattop, and a long ponytail. He has angular strips of facial hair along his cheeks and hair around his mouth and chin. His beard changes between appearances, with his later design featuring a more distinct goatee.

He initially wears a fitted coat with decorative fastenings down the front, pants, and boots. As an executioner, he wears a studded hood, a mask covering his face, gloves, and a sleeveless uniform bearing a fleur-de-lis. At his clinic, he wears a short-sleeved tunic with the same emblem. He puts on a head covering and face mask for surgery.
Color Schemes
Personality: Gregorio is stern, disciplined, and deeply committed to his duties to his family and the monarchy. He teaches Gyro that happiness lies within the family, that protecting one's family serves the country, and that allowing it to fall apart dishonors both one's ancestors and future descendants. He regards the king's orders as God's will and insists that the Zeppelis' responsibility is to carry out sentences accurately, rather than decide whether the condemned are guilty or innocent.

Gregorio treats sentimentality as a weakness that can cause hesitation at a critical moment. To avoid forming emotional attachments, he keeps no personal friends or pets, avoids social gatherings and weddings, and does not write letters or diaries, exchange gifts, or allow himself to be photographed. He does not attend Gyro's school graduation, either. His restraint also extends to his manner of speaking: even when deeply angry with Gyro, he reprimands him quietly rather than shouting.

His severity is tied to his belief that an executioner must avoid inflicting unnecessary suffering. He considers even a slight error in a sword stroke capable of turning a lawful execution into an act of cruelty that dishonors the condemned, the king, and the law. He expects the same composure regardless of a prisoner's age, size, or crime.

Gregorio also believes that doctors must accept limits on their responsibility. When only one of two patients can be saved, he rejects leaving the choice to a relative whose feelings would determine the outcome, insisting that the physicians make the decision themselves. Nevertheless, he believes in miracles and hopes that events beyond human control will turn out favorably.

Despite his strict principles, Gregorio shows empathy as he quietly protects Wekapipo's sister. He explains that her blindness has kept her late husband's influential father from having her killed, and that restoring her sight could have brought about a greater tragedy. Gyro later states that Gregorio is sheltering her in the countryside.
Abilities: Spin

Gregorio is an experienced user of the Spin and Steel Balls. Before an execution, he places a spinning ball on the condemned prisoner's back to quiet his body and allow a precise decapitation. The family's technique was developed to bring peace to the condemned rather than cause pain.

He trains Gyro from childhood, first challenging him to take a Steel Ball from his closed hand. His later instruction includes the golden rectangle, and Gyro credits him with training even his palm to conform to its proportions. Gyro also repeats the family's instruction to "pay your respects" when teaching Johnny to use the technique.
Although the Zeppeli family's traditions describe using a horse's power to strengthen the Spin, Gyro states that he has never seen Gregorio use this technique.
Medicine and Surgery

Gregorio runs a clinic where he treats rich and poor patients alike. His work as an executioner also requires a detailed understanding of anatomy, allowing him to kill with a single accurate stroke. He performs surgery with Gyro as his assistant and instructs him in making difficult decisions when their resources cannot save every patient.
Gyro considers Gregorio a more capable surgeon than himself, believing that his father could have successfully restored Wekapipo's sister's sight after his own attempt fails.

Personality: Gyro's mother is affectionate and attentive to her family. She prepares meals when Gregorio is summoned by the king. She silently kisses the thirteen-year-old Gyro on the cheek before he accompanies his father to the royal prison.

During medical work, she is practical and cautious, urging Gyro to concentrate on the treatment at hand rather than pursue an unrelated problem. Like Gregorio, she believes they should be grateful for saving a patient and avoid unnecessary intervention, warning Gyro against operating on Wekapipo's sister's eyes. Appearance: Marco is a young nine-year-old boy with a small build, soft facial features, and large, dark, expressive eyes. His most distinct feature is his hairstyle, which is short and dark with a unique light quiff at the front. In his first appearance, Marco wears a light-colored collared shirt underneath a pair of dark overalls. When polishing shoes, he wears a dark suit with a bow tie. Personality: Marco is a gentle, obedient, and hardworking boy who takes pride in serving others. Raised in a long line of servants, he was taught by his father to find happiness by remaining humble and diligent. Despite being only nine years old, Marco approaches his duties, which involves shining shoes, brushing hats, and performing household tasks, with genuine enthusiasm and a strong sense of responsibility.

Naive and sheltered, Marco fails to grasp the severity of his circumstances even after being wrongfully arrested and sentenced to death. His instinct is to continue serving, sewing the lost and damaged gorget of his executioner, and responding to accusations with calm sincerity. He doesn't show resentment or fear even when he is misunderstood or punished. He is resourceful, being able to stitch using a needle he made out of a fish bone. Moreover, he is confident in his own abilities, believing that he could fulfill his tasks like shining shoes and silverware better than anyone. Marco also seems to have a good memory, as he claims that he could memorize all of the names of meals and wine.

Personality: Joseph is devoted to Jesus, carefully treating his wounded body with aromatics and wrapping it in linen. When the resurrected Jesus announces his departure, Joseph tearfully asks whether they will meet again.

His devotion also shows in his care for the map Jesus leaves behind. Although neither he nor anyone else understands the land or the nine marks it depicts, Joseph faithfully copies it and safeguards it for the rest of his life.

Appearance: Dario is a man of average height and build. His light-colored hair is shaved on the sides with a tuft in the front, and kept long in the back. In contrast to his fair hair, he sports a dark goatee and sideburns. His eyebrows are also dark and have the same prominent arch as his son's. Typical for a rural peasant, his attire consists of a simple cloak, tunic, and pants. He is also shown wearing cloth bracers on his wrists.
Color Schemes
Personality: Dario is cruel and callous, showing no remorse for infanticide and leaving his family for dead. Although both parents had apparently made the decision together to bury their newborn baby, it can be assumed that it was mainly at Dario's insistence, based on his cruel personality and the fact that he took the most active role in the burial. Prone to flying into a rage, his abusive nature is apparent when he beats his wife for suggesting that his alcoholism is contributing to their poverty. A man void of any sense of responsibility, he sees his wife and child as nothing more than a burden, overjoyed at the prospect of getting rid of them both.

Nicholas is capable of controlling large horses like his own perfectly, no different than when he is riding any other horse.
Personal Skills

Nicholas is never a fraction of a second late. Whether Johnny tells him to run 200 meters in 17 seconds, or the next 200 meters in 23 seconds, he'll always finish exactly in that time. He was born with this ability, unlike his father.

personagens.resumo: Wekapipo's sister (ウェカピポの妹, Wekapipo no Imōto) is an unnamed tertiary character featured in the seventh part of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, Steel Ball Run.

ja_kanji.texto: ウェカピポの妹

family.texto: Unnamed Husband | Unnamed Father-in-Law | Wekapipo (Older Brother)

Appearance: She is a young, light-skinned woman of a petite build. She has long, dark hair with a parted fringe, with the back styled into buns. In the aftermath of her husband's abuse, she wears a long, sleeveless V-neck dress with a dotted pattern. While being operated on by Gyro Zeppeli and his mother, she wears a shorter, short-sleeved dress with a flowered pattern.

During her wedding, she wore a typical, lightly colored wedding gown and veil adorned with a wreath of flowers. In a flashback, she is shown with her hair tied into a braid and wearing an outfit consisting of a dark, collared jacket over a lightly colored skirt wearing a wide brimmed hat.
As a result of her husband's beatings, she was rendered partially blind due to a damaged optic nerve in the back of her left eye, which later becomes full blindness due to a botched surgery by Gyro.
Color Schemes
Personality: The woman displays a level of anxiousness and denial that leaves her vulnerable to her husband's physical and psychological abuse. She is led to believe that her husband's beatings are a fault of her own, and that it is her duty as his wife to behave well, seeing her husband's abuse as retribution for her own failings. Outside of their relationship, her husband describes her as a "boring lay." After Wekapipo discovers her near-blindness due to her husband's abuse, she downplays the severity of her injury by claiming that it is temporary and would heal soon. She expresses a level of affection for her brother and is brought to tears after her husband beats him and challenges him to a duel, to which Wekapipo responds by comforting her and affirming that it would be fine.

After regaining consciousness from her operation by Gyro Zeppeli, she expresses gratitude towards him for mending her injuries despite his failure to cure her blindness and further consoles him by claiming that she hadn't been able to see for some time regardless.

Appearance: Wekapipo's brother-in-law is a clean-shaven man with his hair combed over to the side.
Befitting of his noble status, Wekapipo's brother-in-law wears formal clothing, consisting of a long-sleeved shirt underneath a vest with a neck cloth pants hanging from just below his chest.
While dueling, he wears a knee-length coat, a bowtie at his neck, regular with boots reaching his calf and a holster to hold his Steel Ball.
Color Schemes
Personality: Wekapipo's brother-in-law is shown to be highly abusive, aggressive and cruel towards his wife. Due to his noble status, he takes advantage of his status and takes any dishonor or shame to his family's name personally while maintaining an appearance of nobility by upholding tradition. He chastises Wekapipo's requests that the nobleman divorce his sister for her safety as a divorce, with the church's approval, caused by physical abuse would bring great shame to his family's name. He regards Wekapipo's sister as a "boring lay", regularly using physical violence against her to the point she eventually became blind.

Adding to his dishonorable nature, he accepts to duel Wekapipo as a way for him take responsibility with ulterior motives. He brings several members from the royal guard, including Gregorio Zeppeli, as witnesses to the duel as a ruse to get Wekapipo eliminated by the Kingdom of Naples under the guise of being "observers" to keep the duel fair, resulting in Wekapipo's exile upon winning.
Abilities: Wrecking Ball
As a royal guard member, Wekapipo's brother-in-law possesses a unique type of steel ball that is traditionally wielded by the imperial guard serving the royal family.
